rules.rule_name: New Session Redirect to Sign-On
rules.rule_description: When the program is invoked without any prior session context, the user must be redirected to the Sign-On screen before accessing the User Update function.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1:Session Initialization Check
Redirect to Sign-On Screen COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the User Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: There is no existing session communication area (EIBCALEN = 0), indicating this is a brand new session with no prior context
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to 'COSGN00C' (Sign-On screen) and transfers control to it, preventing access to the User Update screen without a valid session

rules.rule_name: First Entry Screen Initialization
rules.rule_description: On the very first entry into the User Update screen within a session, the screen must be initialized and the session marked as re-entered to distinguish subsequent interactions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is this the first entry into the update screen?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid session exists (communication area is present) and the User Update screen is being accessed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program detects this is the first entry (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER flag is not set)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the session as re-entered (sets CDEMO-PGM-REENTER to TRUE), clears the screen output area (COUSR2AO) to LOW-VALUES, and positions the cursor on the User ID input field

rules.rule_name: Auto-Population of Pre-Selected User ID
rules.rule_description: When a user record was pre-selected from a previous screen (e.g., an admin list), the User ID should be automatically populated and the user's details immediately retrieved and displayed without requiring manual entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2:Initial Screen Load with Pre-selected User
Auto-populate User ID field

acceptance_criteria.Given: This is the first entry into the User Update screen and a User ID has been passed from the previous screen (CDEMO-CU02-USR-SELECTED is not SPACES or LOW-VALUES)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects a pre-selected User ID in the session context
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system copies the pre-selected User ID into the User ID input field (USRIDINI of COUSR2AI) and immediately performs the user lookup process (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY) to retrieve and display the user's details

rules.rule_name: Display User Update Screen with Header
rules.rule_description: Every time the User Update screen is displayed, the header must be populated with current system information including application titles, transaction ID, program name, current date and time.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3:Display User Update Screen
Show form with header, messages, and user fields

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User Update screen is about to be sent to the user's terminal
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to display the screen (SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN is performed)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system populates the screen header with: Application Title lines (CCDA-TITLE01, CCDA-TITLE02), current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID), current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME), current date in MM/DD/YY format (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY), and current time in HH:MM:SS format (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS). Any pending message in WS-MESSAGE is also displayed in the ERRMSGO field. The screen is sent with ERASE and CURSOR options.

rules.rule_name: Capture Operator Input from Screen
rules.rule_description: After the User Update screen has been displayed and the user has interacted with it, the system must receive and capture all input entered by the operator before processing any actions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4:Receive User Input from Screen
Capture operator input

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User Update screen has been displayed and the session is in re-entered state (operator interaction mode)
acceptance_criteria.When: The operator presses any key to submit their input
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system receives all screen input data into the COUSR2AI input map, capturing the values entered in User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type fields, making them available for subsequent processing

rules.rule_name: User ID Empty Validation on Lookup
rules.rule_description: Before performing a user lookup, the User ID field must be validated to ensure it is not empty. This applies both when the Enter key is pressed and when a pre-selected user ID is being processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5:Validate User ID on Lookup
Check if User ID is empty

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has pressed the Enter key or a pre-selected User ID is being processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The User ID input field (USRIDINI of COUSR2AI) contains only SPACES or LOW-VALUES
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), displays the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...' in WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the User ID field (USRIDINL = -1), and redisplays the User Update screen without performing any file lookup

rules.rule_name: User Record Lookup from Security File
rules.rule_description: When a valid User ID is provided, the system must look up the user's record from the User Security file to retrieve their current information for display and potential update.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6:Look Up User Record
Retrieve user from security file

acceptance_criteria.Given: A non-empty User ID has been entered and passed validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a lookup of the User Security file (WS-USRSEC-FILE) using the provided User ID (SEC-USR-ID) as the key, with an UPDATE intent to lock the record for potential modification
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the user record is found successfully: the system retrieves the full user data record (SEC-USER-DATA) including First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type, and displays the message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...' in neutral color. If the User ID is not found in the security file: the error flag is set, the message 'User ID NOT found...' is displayed, and the cursor is positioned on the User ID field. If a system error occurs during lookup: the error flag is set and the message 'Unable to lookup User...' is displayed with cursor on the First Name field.

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen with Retrieved User Data
rules.rule_description: After successfully retrieving a user record from the security file, all user details must be populated on the screen to allow the operator to review and modify them.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7:Populate Screen with Existing User Data
Fill form with current First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the retrieved user data after a successful file read
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system populates the screen input fields with the retrieved values: First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME → FNAMEI of COUSR2AI), Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME → LNAMEI of COUSR2AI), Password (SEC-USR-PWD → PASSWDI of COUSR2AI), and User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE → USRTYPEI of COUSR2AI). The screen is then redisplayed with these populated values and the message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...'

rules.rule_name: Key Press Routing Decision
rules.rule_description: The system must route the operator's interaction to the correct processing function based on which function key was pressed, supporting lookup (Enter), save-and-stay (PF5), save-and-return (PF3), clear (PF4), and cancel (PF12) operations.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Which key did operator press?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has submitted input from the User Update screen and the screen data has been received
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the EIBAID (key pressed indicator)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system routes processing as follows: ENTER key → perform user ID lookup (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY); PF3 key → perform save then navigate back (UPDATE-USER-INFO then RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN); PF4 key → clear all screen fields (CLEAR-CURRENT-SCREEN); PF5 key → perform save and stay on screen (UPDATE-USER-INFO); PF12 key → navigate to Admin Menu without saving (COADM01C via RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN); Any other key → display invalid key error message and redisplay screen

rules.rule_name: Mandatory Field Validation Before Update
rules.rule_description: Before any user record update can be performed, all five required fields must be validated to ensure none are empty. Validation is performed in a specific priority order and stops at the first failure.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8:Validate All Required Fields Before Update
Check User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type are not empty

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF3 or PF5 to initiate a save of user information
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates each required field in sequence
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system validates fields in the following priority order, stopping at the first failure and displaying the corresponding error with cursor positioned on the failing field: (1) If User ID (USRIDINI of COUSR2AI) is SPACES or LOW-VALUES → error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...', cursor on User ID field; (2) If First Name (FNAMEI of COUSR2AI) is SPACES or LOW-VALUES → error message 'First Name can NOT be empty...', cursor on First Name field; (3) If Last Name (LNAMEI of COUSR2AI) is SPACES or LOW-VALUES → error message 'Last Name can NOT be empty...', cursor on Last Name field; (4) If Password (PASSWDI of COUSR2AI) is SPACES or LOW-VALUES → error message 'Password can NOT be empty...', cursor on Password field; (5) If User Type (USRTYPEI of COUSR2AI) is SPACES or LOW-VALUES → error message 'User Type can NOT be empty...', cursor on User Type field. If all fields are valid, processing continues to change detection.

rules.rule_name: Detect Changes to User Data Fields
rules.rule_description: After retrieving the current user record, the system must compare each entered field value against the stored value to determine if any actual changes have been made before attempting to write to the security file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9:Detect Changes to User Data
Compare entered values against current stored values

acceptance_criteria.Given: All required field validations have passed and the current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares each screen input field against the corresponding stored value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system performs field-by-field comparison: If First Name entered (FNAMEI of COUSR2AI) differs from stored First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME) → update SEC-USR-FNAME with new value and set USR-MODIFIED-YES flag; If Last Name entered (LNAMEI of COUSR2AI) differs from stored Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME) → update SEC-USR-LNAME with new value and set USR-MODIFIED-YES flag; If Password entered (PASSWDI of COUSR2AI) differs from stored Password (SEC-USR-PWD) → update SEC-USR-PWD with new value and set USR-MODIFIED-YES flag; If User Type entered (USRTYPEI of COUSR2AI) differs from stored User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE) → update SEC-USR-TYPE with new value and set USR-MODIFIED-YES flag. Multiple fields can be modified in a single operation.

rules.rule_name: Save Updated User Record to Security File
rules.rule_description: When changes to user data have been detected, the updated user record must be written back to the User Security file and the operator notified of the outcome.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10:Save Updated User Information
Write updated record to security file

acceptance_criteria.Given: At least one user data field (First Name, Last Name, Password, or User Type) has been modified and the USR-MODIFIED-YES flag is set
acceptance_criteria.When: The system rewrites the updated user record (SEC-USER-DATA) to the User Security file (WS-USRSEC-FILE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the rewrite is successful: the system clears any prior messages, displays a success confirmation message in GREEN color formatted as 'User [SEC-USR-ID] has been updated...' and redisplays the screen. If the User ID is not found during the rewrite: the error flag is set and the message 'User ID NOT found...' is displayed with cursor on the User ID field. If a system error occurs during the rewrite: the error flag is set and the message 'Unable to Update User...' is displayed with cursor on the First Name field.

rules.rule_name: No Changes Detected Warning
rules.rule_description: If the operator attempts to save user information but has not actually changed any field values from their current stored values, the system must warn the operator and prevent an unnecessary write to the security file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11:No Changes Detected Warning
Display: Please modify to update...
in Red

acceptance_criteria.Given: All required field validations have passed and the current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The comparison of all four fields (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) shows no differences between entered values and stored values (USR-MODIFIED-YES flag remains FALSE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does NOT write to the User Security file, displays the warning message 'Please modify to update...' in RED color (DFHRED) in the ERRMSGC field, and redisplays the User Update screen with the current data intact

rules.rule_name: Save and Return to Previous Screen on PF3
rules.rule_description: When the operator presses PF3, the system must first attempt to save any changes and then navigate the operator back to the appropriate previous screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
12:Save and Return to Previous Screen PF3
Attempt save then navigate back

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF3 on the User Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system completes the save attempt (UPDATE-USER-INFO) regardless of whether changes were made or validation passed
acceptance_criteria.Then: After the save attempt, the system determines the return destination: if a 'from program' is recorded in the session context (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is not SPACES or LOW-VALUES), the operator is returned to that originating program; otherwise, the operator is returned to the Administration Menu screen (COADM01C). Control is transferred via XCTL with the current session communication area preserved.

rules.rule_name: Clear All Screen Fields on PF4
rules.rule_description: When the operator presses PF4, all input fields and messages on the User Update screen must be cleared, allowing the operator to start a fresh user lookup.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
13:Clear Screen Fields PF4
Clear all input fields and messages

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF4 on the User Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the PF4 key press
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears all input fields to SPACES: User ID (USRIDINI of COUSR2AI), First Name (FNAMEI of COUSR2AI), Last Name (LNAMEI of COUSR2AI), Password (PASSWDI of COUSR2AI), and User Type (USRTYPEI of COUSR2AI). The status/error message (WS-MESSAGE) is also cleared to SPACES. The cursor is repositioned to the User ID field (USRIDINL = -1). The screen is redisplayed in its cleared state.

rules.rule_name: Return to Administration Screen Without Saving on PF12
rules.rule_description: When the operator presses PF12, the system must immediately navigate back to the Administration Menu screen without saving any changes, effectively cancelling the update operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
15:Return to Administration Screen PF12
Navigate to COADM01C without saving

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF12 on the User Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the PF12 key press
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does NOT perform any save operation or validation. It sets the destination program to 'COADM01C' (Administration Menu) and immediately transfers control to that program via XCTL with the current session communication area, discarding any unsaved changes on the screen

rules.rule_name: Invalid Key Press Handling
rules.rule_description: If the operator presses any key that is not a supported function key (Enter, PF3, PF4, PF5, PF12), the system must notify the operator that the key is not valid for this screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
16:Invalid Key Handling
Display invalid key message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has pressed a key on the User Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The pressed key is not one of the supported keys: Enter, PF3, PF4, PF5, or PF12
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), populates WS-MESSAGE with the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY), and redisplays the User Update screen with the current field values intact and the error message shown

rules.rule_name: Navigation to Previous or Default Screen
rules.rule_description: When navigating away from the User Update screen, the system must determine the correct destination program and transfer control, defaulting to the Sign-On screen if no destination is specified.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
17:Return to Previous Screen Navigation
Transfer control to calling program or default to sign-on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that navigation away from the User Update screen is required (triggered by PF3, PF12, or new session redirect)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the return-to-previous-screen navigation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system first checks if a destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) has been set; if it is LOW-VALUES or SPACES, it defaults to 'COSGN00C' (Sign-On screen). The system then records the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) as CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) as CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, resets the program context (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) to ZEROS, and transfers control to the destination program via XCTL with the full session communication area

rules.rule_name: Detect Missing Session on Program Launch
rules.rule_description: When the User Update program is launched without an active session context (no communication area passed), the system must detect this condition and prevent access to user update operations by redirecting the user to the Sign-On screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Does a valid session exist?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User Update program (COUSR2) has been launched and no communication area length is present (session length equals zero), indicating no active session exists
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates whether a valid session context was passed at program entry
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system determines that no valid session exists and initiates a redirect to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C), blocking access to all user update operations

rules.rule_name: Assign Sign-On Screen as Redirect Destination When No Session Exists
rules.rule_description: When no valid session is detected at program launch, the system must explicitly set the navigation destination to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) before performing the redirect, ensuring the user is routed to authenticate first.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set destination to Sign-On Screen COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has determined that no valid session context exists (communication area length is zero)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redirect the user away from the User Update screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The destination program is set to the Sign-On screen identifier 'COSGN00C' so that the subsequent navigation targets the correct authentication screen

rules.rule_name: Validate That a Redirect Destination Has Been Assigned
rules.rule_description: Before executing any navigation away from the User Update screen, the system must verify that a valid destination program has been assigned. This safeguard ensures the user is never redirected to an undefined or blank destination.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is destination screen assigned?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is about to redirect the user to a previous or target screen and the destination program field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) has been evaluated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the destination program identifier contains a valid value (i.e., is not blank spaces and not low-values)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the destination program is blank or unassigned (contains spaces or low-values), the system proceeds to apply a default destination; if the destination is already assigned with a valid program name, the system proceeds directly to record navigation details and execute the redirect

rules.rule_name: Default Redirect Destination to Sign-On Screen When Destination Is Missing
rules.rule_description: As a safety policy, if the redirect destination is found to be unassigned or blank at the point of navigation, the system must default the destination to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C), ensuring the user is always routed to a valid and secure screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Default to Sign-On Screen COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is executing the return-to-previous-screen navigation logic and the destination program field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is found to contain spaces or low-values (i.e., no destination was explicitly set)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system applies the default destination rule
acceptance_criteria.Then: The destination program is overridden and set to the Sign-On screen identifier 'COSGN00C', ensuring a valid navigation target is always present before the redirect is executed

rules.rule_name: Record Current Program and Transaction Details for Return Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to another screen, the system must record the current transaction ID, current program name, and reset the program context to zero in the session communication area. This ensures the destination screen knows where the user came from and can support correct back-navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record current program and transaction details for return navigation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has confirmed a valid redirect destination and is preparing to transfer control to another screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system records navigation context details prior to executing the screen transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current transaction identifier (WS-TRANID) is stored as the originating transaction (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is stored as the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), and the program context indicator is reset to zero (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT = 0) in the session communication area

rules.rule_name: Transfer User to Sign-On Screen via Program Control
rules.rule_description: After all navigation details have been recorded, the system must execute the actual transfer of control to the designated destination screen, passing the current session communication area so that session context is preserved across the screen transition.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redirect User to Sign-On Screen COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination program has been confirmed and assigned (defaulted to COSGN00C if previously unset), and the current program and transaction details have been recorded in the session communication area
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the screen transfer to the destination program
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, which is 'COSGN00C' in this flow) and the full session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is passed to the destination screen, ensuring session continuity

rules.rule_name: Detect First Entry into User Update Screen
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the user is accessing the Update User screen for the first time in the current session, and initializes the screen state accordingly.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: First Entry into User Update Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user navigates to the User Update screen and the session communication area is present (session is active)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program detects that the screen has NOT been previously entered in this session (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER flag is not set)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program marks the screen as entered (sets CDEMO-PGM-REENTER to TRUE), clears all screen output fields (COUSR2AO set to LOW-VALUES), and positions the cursor on the User ID input field

rules.rule_name: Check if a User ID Was Pre-selected from a Previous Screen
rules.rule_description: On first entry to the Update User screen, determines whether a User ID was passed from a prior screen (e.g., an admin user list) to decide whether to auto-populate the form or display it empty.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was a User ID already selected from a previous screen?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User Update screen is being loaded for the first time in the current session
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks the pre-selected user value (CDEMO-CU02-USR-SELECTED) passed from the previous screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the pre-selected user value is NOT empty (not SPACES and not LOW-VALUES), the system proceeds to auto-populate the User ID field and look up the user's details; if the pre-selected user value IS empty (SPACES or LOW-VALUES), the system displays an empty update form for manual entry

rules.rule_name: Auto-populate User ID Field from Pre-selected User
rules.rule_description: When a User ID has been pre-selected from a previous screen, that User ID is automatically transferred into the User ID input field on the Update User form, eliminating the need for the user to manually type it.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Auto-populate the User ID field on the form

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User Update screen is being loaded for the first time and a User ID was pre-selected from a previous screen (CDEMO-CU02-USR-SELECTED is not empty)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initializes the Update User form
acceptance_criteria.Then: The pre-selected User ID value (CDEMO-CU02-USR-SELECTED) is automatically copied into the User ID input field (USRIDINI) on the Update User form

rules.rule_name: Trigger Automatic User Record Lookup for Pre-selected User
rules.rule_description: After auto-populating the User ID from a pre-selection, the system automatically initiates a lookup of the user's record in the User Security file without requiring the user to press Enter.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Look Up User Record in User Security File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User ID field has been auto-populated from a pre-selected user on the first entry to the Update User screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initializes the form with the pre-selected User ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system automatically performs the user lookup process (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY) which reads the User Security file using the populated User ID as the search key, retrieving the user's stored record for display

rules.rule_name: Pre-fill Update Form with Existing User Details on Successful Lookup
rules.rule_description: When the user record is successfully found in the User Security file, all editable user details are retrieved and pre-filled into the corresponding fields on the Update User form.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Pre-fill the Update Form with existing user details: First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: A User ID has been looked up in the User Security file and the user record was found successfully (no error flag is set)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system retrieves the user's stored details from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system populates the Update User form with the following fields from the retrieved record: First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME → FNAMEI), Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME → LNAMEI), Password (SEC-USR-PWD → PASSWDI), and User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE → USRTYPEI)

rules.rule_name: Display Update Form with Save Instruction After Successful User Lookup
rules.rule_description: After successfully retrieving and pre-filling the user's details, the system displays the Update User form with an instructional message guiding the user to press PF5 to save any modifications.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Update Form with message: Press PF5 to save updates

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user record has been successfully found in the User Security file and all user details have been pre-filled into the Update User form
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is ready to present the pre-filled form to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Update User screen is displayed with all user fields populated, and the message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates ...' is shown in a neutral color (DFHNEUTR) in the message area, prompting the user to make changes and save

rules.rule_name: Display Error When Pre-selected User ID Is Not Found in Security File
rules.rule_description: When the system attempts to look up a pre-selected User ID in the User Security file but the record does not exist, an error message is displayed to inform the user that the specified User ID was not found.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Update Form with error message: User ID NOT found...

acceptance_criteria.Given: A User ID was pre-selected from a previous screen and the system has attempted to look up that User ID in the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The User Security file lookup returns a 'not found' response (record does not exist for the given User ID)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error flag is set to 'Y' (WS-ERR-FLG), the error message 'User ID NOT found...' is displayed in the message area of the Update User screen, and the cursor is repositioned to the User ID input field to allow the user to enter a different User ID

rules.rule_name: Display Empty Update Form When No User Was Pre-selected
rules.rule_description: When no User ID was pre-selected from a previous screen, the Update User form is displayed empty, allowing the user to manually enter a User ID and look up the user they wish to update.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Empty Update Form for manual entry

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User Update screen is being loaded for the first time in the current session
acceptance_criteria.When: The pre-selected user value (CDEMO-CU02-USR-SELECTED) is empty (SPACES or LOW-VALUES), meaning no user was passed from a previous screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Update User screen is displayed with all input fields empty (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type all blank), the cursor is positioned on the User ID field, and no pre-filled data or instructional message is shown — the user must manually enter a User ID

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Current System Time and Format as HH-MM-SS

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Current System Date and Time / Format Time as HH-MM-SS

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the User Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen display process is initiated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system time, extracts hours (HH), minutes (MM), and seconds (SS), assembles them into HH-MM-SS format, and places the formatted time into the screen header time field (CURTIMEO)

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Header with Application Titles, Transaction ID and Program Name
rules.rule_description: Before displaying the User Update screen, the system populates the screen header with the application title lines, the current transaction identifier, and the current program name to provide context to the operator.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate Screen Header with Transaction ID and Program Name

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the User Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header is being populated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system places the application title line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) into the first title field (TITLE01O), the application title line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) into the second title field (TITLE02O), the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) into the transaction name field (TRNNAMEO), and the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) into the program name field (PGMNAMEO) on the screen header

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Header with Formatted Current Date and Time
rules.rule_description: Before displaying the User Update screen, the system places the formatted current date (MM-DD-YY) and formatted current time (HH-MM-SS) into the corresponding screen header display fields.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate Screen Header with Formatted Current Date and Time

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current date has been formatted as MM-DD-YY and the current time has been formatted as HH-MM-SS
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header is being populated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system places the formatted date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) into the screen date display field (CURDATEO) and the formatted time (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) into the screen time display field (CURTIMEO) in the screen header

rules.rule_name: Display Error or Informational Message on Screen When Present
rules.rule_description: When the User Update screen is displayed, any error or informational message that has been set during processing is transferred to the screen message area so the operator can see it. If no message has been set, the message area remains blank (spaces).
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is there an error or informational message to display? / Place Error or Informational Message in Screen Message Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the User Update screen and a message may or may not have been set in WS-MESSAGE
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: If WS-MESSAGE contains an error or informational message (e.g., 'User ID can NOT be empty...', 'User ID NOT found...', 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...', 'User [UserID] has been updated...', 'Please modify to update...', or an invalid key message), that message is placed into the screen message area (ERRMSGO); if WS-MESSAGE contains only spaces, the screen message area is displayed as blank

rules.rule_name: Display User Update Form with All User Data Fields to Operator
rules.rule_description: After all header and message information has been populated, the complete User Update form is presented to the operator. The form displays all user data fields — User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type — along with the populated header and any message, and positions the cursor appropriately for operator input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display User Update Form to Operator with all fields: User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen header has been populated with current date, time, transaction ID, and program name, and any applicable message has been placed in the message area
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the User Update screen to the operator's terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User Update form (map COUSR2A from mapset COUSR02) is displayed to the operator showing all user data fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type), the populated header information, and any error or informational message; the screen is fully refreshed (erased and rewritten) and the cursor is positioned at the designated input field

rules.rule_name: Capture Operator Input from User Update Form
rules.rule_description: When an operator submits the User Update Form, the system must capture all data entered on the screen — including User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type — from the User Update screen map (COUSR2A) into the internal input area for further processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Data Entered by Operator from User Update Form

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has previously been presented with the User Update Form (the program is in re-entry mode, meaning the screen has already been displayed at least once in the current session)
acceptance_criteria.When: The operator submits the User Update Form by pressing any key (Enter, PF3, PF4, PF5, PF12, or any other key)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system captures all data entered by the operator from the User Update screen map (COUSR2A / COUSR02 mapset) into the internal input data area (COUSR2AI), making the following fields available for processing: User ID (USRIDINI), First Name (FNAMEI), Last Name (LNAMEI), Password (PASSWDI), and User Type (USRTYPEI)

rules.rule_name: Receive User ID Field from User Update Form
rules.rule_description: The User ID field entered by the operator on the User Update Form is received as part of the screen data capture. This field identifies which user record is to be looked up or updated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Receive User ID Field Entered by Operator

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has submitted the User Update Form and the system is capturing screen input from the User Update screen map (COUSR2A)
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen data is received into the internal input area (COUSR2AI)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID value entered by the operator is available in the USRIDINI field of the input area, ready to be used for user record lookup or update validation

rules.rule_name: Receive First Name Field from User Update Form
rules.rule_description: The First Name field entered or modified by the operator on the User Update Form is received as part of the screen data capture. This field represents the user's first name to be updated in the User Security file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Receive First Name Field Entered or Modified by Operator

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has submitted the User Update Form and the system is capturing screen input from the User Update screen map (COUSR2A)
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen data is received into the internal input area (COUSR2AI)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The First Name value entered or modified by the operator is available in the FNAMEI field of the input area, ready to be compared against the existing stored value and potentially saved to the User Security file

rules.rule_name: Receive Last Name Field from User Update Form
rules.rule_description: The Last Name field entered or modified by the operator on the User Update Form is received as part of the screen data capture. This field represents the user's last name to be updated in the User Security file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Receive Last Name Field Entered or Modified by Operator

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has submitted the User Update Form and the system is capturing screen input from the User Update screen map (COUSR2A)
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen data is received into the internal input area (COUSR2AI)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Last Name value entered or modified by the operator is available in the LNAMEI field of the input area, ready to be compared against the existing stored value and potentially saved to the User Security file

rules.rule_name: Receive Password Field from User Update Form
rules.rule_description: The Password field entered or modified by the operator on the User Update Form is received as part of the screen data capture. This field represents the user's password to be updated in the User Security file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Receive Password Field Entered or Modified by Operator

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has submitted the User Update Form and the system is capturing screen input from the User Update screen map (COUSR2A)
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen data is received into the internal input area (COUSR2AI)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Password value entered or modified by the operator is available in the PASSWDI field of the input area, ready to be compared against the existing stored value and potentially saved to the User Security file

rules.rule_name: Receive User Type Field from User Update Form
rules.rule_description: The User Type field entered or modified by the operator on the User Update Form is received as part of the screen data capture. This field represents the user's role or type classification to be updated in the User Security file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Receive User Type Field Entered or Modified by Operator

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has submitted the User Update Form and the system is capturing screen input from the User Update screen map (COUSR2A)
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen data is received into the internal input area (COUSR2AI)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User Type value entered or modified by the operator is available in the USRTYPEI field of the input area, ready to be compared against the existing stored value and potentially saved to the User Security file

rules.rule_name: Route Processing Based on Key Pressed After Input Capture
rules.rule_description: Once all operator input has been successfully captured from the User Update Form, the system determines the appropriate processing action based on which function key the operator pressed when submitting the form. Each key triggers a distinct business operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Process Operator's Request based on Key Pressed

acceptance_criteria.Given: All operator input has been successfully captured from the User Update Form into the internal input area (COUSR2AI)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the function key pressed by the operator at the time of form submission
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system routes processing as follows: if the operator pressed Enter — perform a User ID lookup to retrieve and display the user's current details; if the operator pressed PF3 — save any changes to the user record and then navigate back to the previous screen; if the operator pressed PF4 — clear all fields on the screen and redisplay an empty form; if the operator pressed PF5 — save any changes to the user record and remain on the User Update screen; if the operator pressed PF12 — navigate back to the Admin Menu without saving any changes; if any other key was pressed — display an invalid key error message and redisplay the current screen with all entered data intact

rules.rule_name: Validate User ID is Not Empty Before Lookup
rules.rule_description: When an operator presses Enter to look up a user record, the system must validate that the User ID field has been entered. If the User ID field is blank or contains no value, the system must prevent the lookup, display an error message, and prompt the operator to provide a valid User ID before proceeding.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is the User ID field empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator is on the Update User screen and has pressed the Enter key to initiate a user record lookup
acceptance_criteria.When: The User ID input field is empty (contains only spaces or no value at all)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the error flag to ON to indicate a validation failure, (2) Display the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...' on the screen, (3) Position the cursor on the User ID input field to guide the operator, (4) Redisplay the Update User screen with the error message visible, and (5) NOT proceed to look up any user record — the operator must enter a valid User ID before the lookup can continue

rules.rule_name: Set User ID as Search Key for Security File Lookup
rules.rule_description: Before searching the User Security File, the User ID entered by the operator on the update form must be assigned as the search key to identify the target user record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use entered User ID to search User Security File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has entered a User ID on the User Update screen and pressed Enter
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to look up the user record in the User Security File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The entered User ID from the update form (USRIDINI) is assigned as the record search key (SEC-USR-ID) to be used for the User Security File lookup

rules.rule_name: Retrieve User Record from User Security File
rules.rule_description: The system must search the User Security File using the provided User ID to retrieve the existing user record. The record is retrieved in update mode to allow subsequent modifications.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use entered User ID to search User Security File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User ID has been set as the search key (SEC-USR-ID) for the User Security File lookup
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs the user record lookup against the User Security File (USRSEC)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system searches the User Security File using the User ID as the record identifier and retrieves the full user data record (SEC-USER-DATA) if it exists, locking it for potential update

rules.rule_name: Populate Update Form with Retrieved User Data
rules.rule_description: When a user record is successfully found in the User Security File, the system must populate all editable fields on the User Update screen with the current stored values for that user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve User Details First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User Security File lookup has completed successfully and the user record was found
acceptance_criteria.When: No error condition is active (ERR-FLG-ON is false)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system populates the User Update screen fields with the retrieved user data: First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME → FNAMEI), Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME → LNAMEI), Password (SEC-USR-PWD → PASSWDI), and User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE → USRTYPEI), and the updated screen is displayed to the operator

rules.rule_name: Display Save Prompt Message After Successful User Lookup
rules.rule_description: When a user record is successfully found and retrieved from the User Security File, the system must guide the operator by displaying an instructional message to press PF5 to save any modifications.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Message: 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User Security File lookup has completed and the user record was found successfully
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the successful lookup response
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the screen message to 'Press PF5 key to save your updates ...' displayed in neutral color, and the User Update screen is refreshed to show this message along with the retrieved user data

rules.rule_name: Display Error When User ID Not Found in Security File
rules.rule_description: When the entered User ID does not match any existing record in the User Security File, the system must notify the operator with a specific error message and direct them to correct the User ID.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Error Message: 'User ID NOT found...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has entered a User ID and the system has searched the User Security File
acceptance_criteria.When: The User Security File lookup returns a 'record not found' result for the entered User ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active ('Y'), displays the error message 'User ID NOT found...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the User ID field to prompt correction, and redisplays the User Update screen

rules.rule_name: Highlight User ID Field for Correction After Not Found Error
rules.rule_description: When a User ID is not found in the User Security File, the system must direct the operator's attention back to the User ID field by positioning the cursor there, enabling immediate correction without additional navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Highlight User ID Field for Correction

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User Security File lookup has returned a 'not found' result for the entered User ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the User Update screen with the error condition
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor length indicator for the User ID field (USRIDINL) is set to -1, which positions the cursor on the User ID input field when the screen is redisplayed, prompting the operator to re-enter a valid User ID

acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the User Update screen for display

rules.rule_name: Mandatory Field Validation Before Saving User Updates
rules.rule_description: Before saving any user updates, the system validates that all required fields are populated. Each field is checked in sequence and the first empty field encountered triggers an error message with cursor placement on that field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: All Required Fields Validation Passed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF5 or PF3 to save user information on the Update User screen

acceptance_criteria.When: The system looks up the User Security file using the entered User ID

rules.rule_description: Before saving user updates, the system must verify that the User ID field has been provided. The User ID is the key identifier for the user record and cannot be blank.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is User ID empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF5 to save user updates on the Update User screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The User ID field is empty or contains only spaces
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag ON, displays the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the User ID field, redisplays the Update User screen, and does not proceed with any further validation or save operation

rules.rule_name: Validate First Name is Not Empty Before Saving
rules.rule_description: Before saving user updates, the system must verify that the First Name field has been provided. First Name is a mandatory attribute of a user record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is First Name empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF5 to save user updates, and the User ID field is not empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The First Name field is empty or contains only spaces
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag ON, displays the error message 'First Name can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the First Name field, redisplays the Update User screen, and does not proceed with any further validation or save operation

rules.rule_name: Validate Last Name is Not Empty Before Saving
rules.rule_description: Before saving user updates, the system must verify that the Last Name field has been provided. Last Name is a mandatory attribute of a user record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Last Name empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF5 to save user updates, and both User ID and First Name fields are not empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The Last Name field is empty or contains only spaces
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag ON, displays the error message 'Last Name can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the Last Name field, redisplays the Update User screen, and does not proceed with any further validation or save operation

rules.rule_name: Validate Password is Not Empty Before Saving
rules.rule_description: Before saving user updates, the system must verify that the Password field has been provided. Password is a mandatory security attribute of a user record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Password empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF5 to save user updates, and User ID, First Name, and Last Name fields are all not empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The Password field is empty or contains only spaces
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag ON, displays the error message 'Password can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the Password field, redisplays the Update User screen, and does not proceed with any further validation or save operation

rules.rule_name: Validate User Type is Not Empty Before Saving
rules.rule_description: Before saving user updates, the system must verify that the User Type field has been provided. User Type is a mandatory classification attribute of a user record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is User Type empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF5 to save user updates, and User ID, First Name, Last Name, and Password fields are all not empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The User Type field is empty or contains only spaces
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag ON, displays the error message 'User Type can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the User Type field, redisplays the Update User screen, and does not proceed with any further validation or save operation

rules.rule_name: Look Up Current User Record from User Security File
rules.rule_description: After all required fields pass validation, the system retrieves the current user record from the User Security file using the entered User ID, to enable field-level comparison before saving updates.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Look Up Current User Record in User Security File

acceptance_criteria.Given: All required fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) have passed validation and no error flag is set
acceptance_criteria.When: The system looks up the user record in the User Security file using the entered User ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the user record is found, the system retrieves the current stored values for First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type, displays the message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...' and proceeds to compare the screen values against the stored values; if the User ID is not found in the User Security file, the system displays the error message 'User ID NOT found...' and positions the cursor on the User ID field; if a system error occurs during the lookup, the system displays the error message 'Unable to lookup User...' and positions the cursor on the First Name field

rules.rule_name: Detect Change in First Name Field
rules.rule_description: After retrieving the current user record, the system compares the First Name entered on screen against the stored First Name value to determine if an update is needed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: First Name changed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The First Name value entered on the screen is different from the First Name currently stored in the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system updates the user record's First Name with the new value from the screen and marks the user record as modified

rules.rule_name: Detect Change in Last Name Field
rules.rule_description: After retrieving the current user record, the system compares the Last Name entered on screen against the stored Last Name value to determine if an update is needed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Last Name changed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The Last Name value entered on the screen is different from the Last Name currently stored in the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system updates the user record's Last Name with the new value from the screen and marks the user record as modified

rules.rule_name: Detect Change in Password Field
rules.rule_description: After retrieving the current user record, the system compares the Password entered on screen against the stored Password value to determine if an update is needed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Password changed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The Password value entered on the screen is different from the Password currently stored in the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system updates the user record's Password with the new value from the screen and marks the user record as modified

rules.rule_name: Detect Change in User Type Field
rules.rule_description: After retrieving the current user record, the system compares the User Type entered on screen against the stored User Type value to determine if an update is needed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: User Type changed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The User Type value entered on the screen is different from the User Type currently stored in the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system updates the user record's User Type with the new value from the screen and marks the user record as modified

rules.rule_name: Determine Whether Any User Fields Were Modified
rules.rule_description: After comparing all individual fields, the system determines whether at least one field was changed to decide whether to proceed with saving or to warn the operator that no changes were detected.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Were any fields modified?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed comparing all four fields (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) between the screen input and the stored user record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether any of the four fields were marked as modified
acceptance_criteria.Then: If at least one field was modified, the system proceeds to save the updated user record to the User Security file; if no fields were modified, the system displays the warning message 'Please modify to update...' in red on the Update User screen and does not perform any save operation

rules.rule_name: Save Updated User Record to User Security File
rules.rule_description: When at least one field has been modified, the system writes the updated user record back to the User Security file to persist the changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save Updated User Record to User Security File

acceptance_criteria.Given: At least one user field (First Name, Last Name, Password, or User Type) has been modified and marked for update
acceptance_criteria.When: The system saves the updated user record to the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the save is successful, the system displays a success confirmation message in green reading 'User [User ID] has been updated...' on the Update User screen; if the User ID is not found during the save, the system displays the error message 'User ID NOT found...' and positions the cursor on the User ID field; if a system error occurs during the save, the system displays the error message 'Unable to Update User...' and positions the cursor on the First Name field

rules.rule_name: Display Success Confirmation After Saving User Updates
rules.rule_description: Upon successfully saving the updated user record, the system provides a clear visual confirmation to the operator that the update was completed successfully.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Success Message in Green: User ID has been updated...

acceptance_criteria.Given: The updated user record has been successfully written to the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The save operation completes without errors
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays a success message in green color formatted as 'User [User ID] has been updated...' on the Update User screen, and the operator remains on the Update User screen

rules.rule_name: Display Warning When No User Fields Were Changed
rules.rule_description: If the operator attempts to save but has not changed any field values from what is already stored, the system warns the operator that a modification is required before an update can be performed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Warning Message in Red: Please modify to update...

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has compared all fields and determined that none of the values (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) differ from the currently stored values in the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: No fields have been marked as modified
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the warning message 'Please modify to update...' in red color on the Update User screen, does not write any record to the User Security file, and the operator remains on the Update User screen

rules.rule_name: Use Entered User ID as Search Key for Update Verification Lookup
rules.rule_description: Before looking up a user record for update, the system must capture the User ID value entered by the operator on the Update User form and use it as the key to search the User Security File.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Take the User ID entered by the operator on the form

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has entered a User ID value in the User ID field on the Update User form and all mandatory field validations have passed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to look up the user record in the User Security File for update verification
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must use the User ID value entered by the operator on the form (USRIDINI field) as the search key (SEC-USR-ID) to locate the corresponding user record in the User Security File

rules.rule_name: Search and Lock User Record in User Security File for Update
rules.rule_description: The system must search the User Security File using the provided User ID and acquire an exclusive lock on the record to prevent concurrent modifications during the update process.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Search for the User ID in the User Security File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has provided a User ID on the Update User form and the system is ready to retrieve the user record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system searches the User Security File (USRSEC) using the User ID as the record key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must read the user record from the User Security File with an exclusive update lock applied, ensuring the record is reserved for this update operation and cannot be modified by another process simultaneously

rules.rule_name: Determine Outcome Based on Whether User Record Was Found
rules.rule_description: After searching the User Security File, the system must evaluate whether the User ID exists in the file and route the process accordingly — either proceeding with the update or notifying the operator of the failure.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was the User Record Found?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has searched the User Security File using the entered User ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The search operation completes
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the user record is found successfully, the system must lock the record and proceed to display the current user data for comparison and update; if the user record is not found, the system must display an error and prompt the operator to re-enter the User ID; if a system error occurs during the search, the system must display an error message indicating the user could not be looked up

rules.rule_name: Lock User Record and Prompt Operator to Save Updates
rules.rule_description: When the user record is successfully found in the User Security File, the system locks the record for exclusive update access and instructs the operator to press PF5 to save their modifications.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Lock the User Record for Update

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully located the user record in the User Security File using the entered User ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The user record is found and the read-with-lock operation completes successfully
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must lock the user record to prevent concurrent updates, display the message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...' in a neutral color on the Update User form, and return the current user data (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) to the form so the operator can review and modify the values

rules.rule_name: Display Save Prompt Message After Successful User Record Retrieval
rules.rule_description: Upon successfully retrieving and locking the user record, the system must guide the operator by displaying an instructional message indicating how to save their changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Message: Press PF5 key to save your updates...

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user record has been successfully found and locked in the User Security File
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to display the Update User form with the retrieved user data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...' in neutral color in the message area of the Update User form, and populate the form fields with the retrieved values: First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME), Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME), Password (SEC-USR-PWD), and User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE)

rules.rule_name: Display User Not Found Error When User ID Does Not Exist in Security File
rules.rule_description: When the entered User ID cannot be located in the User Security File during the update lookup, the system must notify the operator with a specific error message and highlight the User ID field for correction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Error Message: User ID NOT found...

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has entered a User ID on the Update User form and the system has searched the User Security File
acceptance_criteria.When: The User ID is not found in the User Security File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the error indicator to active ('Y'), display the error message 'User ID NOT found...' in the message area of the Update User form, and position the cursor on the User ID field to prompt the operator to enter a valid User ID

rules.rule_name: Return Update Form with Error Highlighted on User ID Field When User Not Found
rules.rule_description: After a failed user lookup due to a non-existent User ID, the system must redisplay the Update User form with the error message visible and the cursor positioned on the User ID field so the operator can correct the entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return to Update Form with error highlighted on User ID field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User ID entered by the operator was not found in the User Security File and the error flag has been set
acceptance_criteria.When: The system redisplays the Update User form
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the Update User form with the error message 'User ID NOT found...' shown in the message area, the cursor positioned on the User ID input field (cursor length set to -1 on USRIDINL), and the header information (current date, time, transaction ID, program name) refreshed on the form

rules.rule_name: Return Update Form with Current User Data Ready for Comparison
rules.rule_description: After successfully retrieving the user record, the system must populate the Update User form with the current stored values so the operator can review and modify them before saving.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return to Update Form with current user data ready for comparison

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user record has been successfully found and locked in the User Security File
acceptance_criteria.When: The system redisplays the Update User form after a successful lookup
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must populate the Update User form fields with the current stored values from the User Security File: First Name field with SEC-USR-FNAME, Last Name field with SEC-USR-LNAME, Password field with SEC-USR-PWD, and User Type field with SEC-USR-TYPE, along with the instructional message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...' so the operator can compare and modify the values before saving

rules.rule_name: Set Destination to Administration Screen on PF12
rules.rule_description: When the operator presses PF12, the system sets the navigation destination to the main Administration Screen (COADM01C) without performing any save operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Destination to Administration Screen COADM01C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator is on the User Update screen with or without unsaved changes
acceptance_criteria.When: The operator presses the PF12 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Administration Screen (COADM01C) and no user data is saved or updated

rules.rule_name: Validate Destination Screen is Not Blank Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before navigating away from the User Update screen, the system validates that a destination screen has been set. If the destination is blank or uninitialized, the system defaults to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to ensure the operator is always directed to a valid screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is destination screen valid?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is about to navigate away from the User Update screen after PF12 is pressed and the destination program field has been set to COADM01C
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the destination program field contains a valid (non-blank, non-empty) value
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the destination program is blank or uninitialized (LOW-VALUES or SPACES), the system overrides it and sets the destination to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C); if the destination is already set to a valid value such as COADM01C, the system retains that destination and proceeds with navigation

rules.rule_name: Preserve and Pass Current Session Context to Destination Screen
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the destination screen, the system records the current transaction identity and program name into the session communication area, and resets the program context indicator to zero, ensuring the destination screen receives accurate session origin information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Pass Current Session and Communication Data to Destination Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination screen has been determined (either COADM01C or defaulted to COSGN00C) and the system is preparing to navigate
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the session communication data for transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction ID into the session's 'from transaction' field, records the current program name into the session's 'from program' field, resets the program context indicator to zero, and packages the full communication area to be passed to the destination screen

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Destination Screen Without Saving Changes
rules.rule_description: After setting the destination and preparing the session context, the system transfers full control to the destination screen (COADM01C or COSGN00C as fallback), passing the complete communication area. Any unsaved changes on the User Update screen are discarded as no save operation is performed during PF12 navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Navigate to Administration Screen COADM01C No Changes Saved

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination screen is confirmed as COADM01C (or COSGN00C as fallback) and the session communication data has been prepared with the current transaction ID, program name, and reset context
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the navigation transfer to the destination program
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is fully transferred to the destination screen with the communication area passed along, the User Update screen is exited, and no changes to user data (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) are saved

rules.rule_name: Detect Unsupported Key Press and Set Error State
rules.rule_description: When an operator presses a key that is not one of the supported function keys (Enter, PF3, PF4, PF5, PF12) on the User Update screen, the system must recognize it as an invalid action and activate the error state to prevent any unintended processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is the key one of the supported keys? Enter, PF3, PF4, PF5, PF12

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator is on the User Update screen and the system is ready to receive a key press
acceptance_criteria.When: The operator presses any key other than Enter, PF3, PF4, PF5, or PF12
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the Error Flag to active ('Y') to indicate an invalid key was pressed, blocking any further data processing actions

rules.rule_name: Load Invalid Key Error Message
rules.rule_description: When an unsupported key is detected, the system must load the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) into the screen message area to inform the operator which keys are valid.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Load Invalid Key Message CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY

acceptance_criteria.Given: The operator has pressed an unsupported key on the User Update screen and the error flag has been set
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the unsupported key event
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system loads the standard invalid key message from CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY into the screen message field (WS-MESSAGE) to be displayed to the operator

rules.rule_name: Redisplay User Update Screen with Invalid Key Error Message
rules.rule_description: After detecting an unsupported key press and loading the invalid key message, the system must redisplay the User Update screen with the error message visible, along with refreshed header information (current date, time, transaction ID, and program name), so the operator can review valid key options and take appropriate action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 3: Redisplay User Update Screen with Invalid Key Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error flag is active and the invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) has been loaded into the message field, and the operator is on the User Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the User Update screen back to the operator
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system populates the screen header with the current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction ID, and program name; places the invalid key error message in the error message display area (ERRMSGO) of the User Update screen (map COUSR2A, mapset COUSR02); and redisplays the screen with all previously entered data intact so the operator can review the valid key options

rules.rule_name: Default to Sign-On Screen When No Calling Program Is Identified
rules.rule_description: When the system needs to return to a previous screen but no originating calling program has been recorded in the session, the destination defaults to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Default destination: Sign-On Screen COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Update User screen and a navigation-back action has been triggered, AND the session data contains no identified calling program (destination program is empty or uninitialized)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the destination program stored in the session communication area and finds it is blank or uninitialized
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) as the default navigation target

rules.rule_name: Use Identified Calling Program as Navigation Destination
rules.rule_description: When the system needs to return to a previous screen and a valid originating calling program is recorded in the session, that program is used as the navigation destination. The calling program may be explicitly set based on the key pressed (PF3 uses the originating program or defaults to Admin Menu; PF12 always uses Admin Menu).
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use the identified calling program as destination

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Update User screen and a navigation-back action has been triggered via PF3 or PF12, AND the session data contains a valid identified calling program or a specific destination has been assigned
acceptance_criteria.When: PF3 is pressed and a valid originating program is recorded in the session, the originating program is set as the destination; if no originating program is recorded, the Admin Menu (COADM01C) is set as the destination. When PF12 is pressed, the Admin Menu (COADM01C) is always set as the destination regardless of the originating program
acceptance_criteria.Then: The destination program in the session communication area is set to the identified calling program (originating program or Admin Menu COADM01C as applicable), and navigation proceeds to that destination

rules.rule_name: Stamp Current Transaction ID and Program Name into Session Data Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the destination program, the system records the current transaction identifier and the current program name into the session communication area. This ensures the destination program knows which transaction and program initiated the navigation, maintaining a complete session trail.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Stamp current Transaction ID and Program Name into session data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined the destination program for navigation and is preparing to transfer control
acceptance_criteria.When: The return-to-previous-screen process is executing
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current Transaction ID is recorded as the originating transaction in the session data, AND the current Program Name is recorded as the originating program in the session data

rules.rule_name: Reset Program Context to Fresh State Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the destination program, the system resets the program context indicator in the session data to zero (fresh/initial state). This ensures the destination program starts without inheriting any stale context flags from the current screen interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset program context to fresh state

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has stamped the current transaction ID and program name into the session data and is preparing to transfer control to the destination program
acceptance_criteria.When: The return-to-previous-screen process is executing
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program context value in the session communication area is reset to zero, clearing any prior context state so the destination program begins in a clean initial state

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Destination Program with Full Session Data
rules.rule_description: As the final step of the return navigation, the system transfers full control to the resolved destination program, passing along the complete session communication area. This ensures the destination program has access to all session context, including the originating transaction, program identity, and any other session state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer control to destination program with session data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination program has been resolved (either the identified calling program or the default Sign-On screen COSGN00C), the current transaction ID and program name have been stamped into the session data, and the program context has been reset to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The return-to-previous-screen process completes its preparation steps
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is fully transferred to the destination program, and the complete session communication area (containing transaction ID, program name, program context, and all other session data) is passed to the destination program; the current program ceases execution

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the User Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: There is no existing session communication area (EIBCALEN = 0), indicating this is a brand new session with no prior context
