Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to 'COSGN00C' (Sign-On screen) and transfers control to it, preventing access to the User Update screen without a valid session

all_rules.Rule_Name: New Session Redirect to Sign-On
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is invoked without any prior session context, the user must be redirected to the Sign-On screen before accessing the User Update function.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid session exists (communication area is present) and the User Update screen is being accessed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program detects this is the first entry (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER flag is not set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the session as re-entered (sets CDEMO-PGM-REENTER to TRUE), clears the screen output area (COUSR2AO) to LOW-VALUES, and positions the cursor on the User ID input field

all_rules.Rule_Name: First Entry Screen Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: On the very first entry into the User Update screen within a session, the screen must be initialized and the session marked as re-entered to distinguish subsequent interactions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: This is the first entry into the User Update screen and a User ID has been passed from the previous screen (CDEMO-CU02-USR-SELECTED is not SPACES or LOW-VALUES)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects a pre-selected User ID in the session context
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the pre-selected User ID into the User ID input field (USRIDINI of COUSR2AI) and immediately performs the user lookup process (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY) to retrieve and display the user's details

all_rules.Rule_Name: Auto-Population of Pre-Selected User ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user record was pre-selected from a previous screen (e.g., an admin list), the User ID should be automatically populated and the user's details immediately retrieved and displayed without requiring manual entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Update screen is about to be sent to the user's terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to display the screen (SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN is performed)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the screen header with: Application Title lines (CCDA-TITLE01, CCDA-TITLE02), current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID), current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME), current date in MM/DD/YY format (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY), and current time in HH:MM:SS format (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS). Any pending message in WS-MESSAGE is also displayed in the ERRMSGO field. The screen is sent with ERASE and CURSOR options.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display User Update Screen with Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every time the User Update screen is displayed, the header must be populated with current system information including application titles, transaction ID, program name, current date and time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Update screen has been displayed and the session is in re-entered state (operator interaction mode)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The operator presses any key to submit their input
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system receives all screen input data into the COUSR2AI input map, capturing the values entered in User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type fields, making them available for subsequent processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Operator Input from Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the User Update screen has been displayed and the user has interacted with it, the system must receive and capture all input entered by the operator before processing any actions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed the Enter key or a pre-selected User ID is being processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID input field (USRIDINI of COUSR2AI) contains only SPACES or LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), displays the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...' in WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the User ID field (USRIDINL = -1), and redisplays the User Update screen without performing any file lookup

all_rules.Rule_Name: User ID Empty Validation on Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before performing a user lookup, the User ID field must be validated to ensure it is not empty. This applies both when the Enter key is pressed and when a pre-selected user ID is being processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A non-empty User ID has been entered and passed validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a lookup of the User Security file (WS-USRSEC-FILE) using the provided User ID (SEC-USR-ID) as the key, with an UPDATE intent to lock the record for potential modification
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the user record is found successfully: the system retrieves the full user data record (SEC-USER-DATA) including First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type, and displays the message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...' in neutral color. If the User ID is not found in the security file: the error flag is set, the message 'User ID NOT found...' is displayed, and the cursor is positioned on the User ID field. If a system error occurs during lookup: the error flag is set and the message 'Unable to lookup User...' is displayed with cursor on the First Name field.

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Record Lookup from Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid User ID is provided, the system must look up the user's record from the User Security file to retrieve their current information for display and potential update.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the retrieved user data after a successful file read
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the screen input fields with the retrieved values: First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME → FNAMEI of COUSR2AI), Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME → LNAMEI of COUSR2AI), Password (SEC-USR-PWD → PASSWDI of COUSR2AI), and User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE → USRTYPEI of COUSR2AI). The screen is then redisplayed with these populated values and the message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen with Retrieved User Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving a user record from the security file, all user details must be populated on the screen to allow the operator to review and modify them.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has submitted input from the User Update screen and the screen data has been received
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the EIBAID (key pressed indicator)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system routes processing as follows: ENTER key → perform user ID lookup (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY); PF3 key → perform save then navigate back (UPDATE-USER-INFO then RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN); PF4 key → clear all screen fields (CLEAR-CURRENT-SCREEN); PF5 key → perform save and stay on screen (UPDATE-USER-INFO); PF12 key → navigate to Admin Menu without saving (COADM01C via RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN); Any other key → display invalid key error message and redisplay screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Key Press Routing Decision
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must route the operator's interaction to the correct processing function based on which function key was pressed, supporting lookup (Enter), save-and-stay (PF5), save-and-return (PF3), clear (PF4), and cancel (PF12) operations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF3 or PF5 to initiate a save of user information
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates each required field in sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system validates fields in the following priority order, stopping at the first failure and displaying the corresponding error with cursor positioned on the failing field: (1) If User ID (USRIDINI of COUSR2AI) is SPACES or LOW-VALUES → error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...', cursor on User ID field; (2) If First Name (FNAMEI of COUSR2AI) is SPACES or LOW-VALUES → error message 'First Name can NOT be empty...', cursor on First Name field; (3) If Last Name (LNAMEI of COUSR2AI) is SPACES or LOW-VALUES → error message 'Last Name can NOT be empty...', cursor on Last Name field; (4) If Password (PASSWDI of COUSR2AI) is SPACES or LOW-VALUES → error message 'Password can NOT be empty...', cursor on Password field; (5) If User Type (USRTYPEI of COUSR2AI) is SPACES or LOW-VALUES → error message 'User Type can NOT be empty...', cursor on User Type field. If all fields are valid, processing continues to change detection.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mandatory Field Validation Before Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any user record update can be performed, all five required fields must be validated to ensure none are empty. Validation is performed in a specific priority order and stops at the first failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All required field validations have passed and the current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares each screen input field against the corresponding stored value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system performs field-by-field comparison: If First Name entered (FNAMEI of COUSR2AI) differs from stored First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME) → update SEC-USR-FNAME with new value and set USR-MODIFIED-YES flag; If Last Name entered (LNAMEI of COUSR2AI) differs from stored Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME) → update SEC-USR-LNAME with new value and set USR-MODIFIED-YES flag; If Password entered (PASSWDI of COUSR2AI) differs from stored Password (SEC-USR-PWD) → update SEC-USR-PWD with new value and set USR-MODIFIED-YES flag; If User Type entered (USRTYPEI of COUSR2AI) differs from stored User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE) → update SEC-USR-TYPE with new value and set USR-MODIFIED-YES flag. Multiple fields can be modified in a single operation.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Changes to User Data Fields
all_rules.Rule_Description: After retrieving the current user record, the system must compare each entered field value against the stored value to determine if any actual changes have been made before attempting to write to the security file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: At least one user data field (First Name, Last Name, Password, or User Type) has been modified and the USR-MODIFIED-YES flag is set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system rewrites the updated user record (SEC-USER-DATA) to the User Security file (WS-USRSEC-FILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the rewrite is successful: the system clears any prior messages, displays a success confirmation message in GREEN color formatted as 'User [SEC-USR-ID] has been updated...' and redisplays the screen. If the User ID is not found during the rewrite: the error flag is set and the message 'User ID NOT found...' is displayed with cursor on the User ID field. If a system error occurs during the rewrite: the error flag is set and the message 'Unable to Update User...' is displayed with cursor on the First Name field.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Updated User Record to Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When changes to user data have been detected, the updated user record must be written back to the User Security file and the operator notified of the outcome.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All required field validations have passed and the current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The comparison of all four fields (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) shows no differences between entered values and stored values (USR-MODIFIED-YES flag remains FALSE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does NOT write to the User Security file, displays the warning message 'Please modify to update...' in RED color (DFHRED) in the ERRMSGC field, and redisplays the User Update screen with the current data intact

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Changes Detected Warning
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the operator attempts to save user information but has not actually changed any field values from their current stored values, the system must warn the operator and prevent an unnecessary write to the security file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF3 on the User Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes the save attempt (UPDATE-USER-INFO) regardless of whether changes were made or validation passed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: After the save attempt, the system determines the return destination: if a 'from program' is recorded in the session context (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is not SPACES or LOW-VALUES), the operator is returned to that originating program; otherwise, the operator is returned to the Administration Menu screen (COADM01C). Control is transferred via XCTL with the current session communication area preserved.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save and Return to Previous Screen on PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the operator presses PF3, the system must first attempt to save any changes and then navigate the operator back to the appropriate previous screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF4 on the User Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the PF4 key press
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears all input fields to SPACES: User ID (USRIDINI of COUSR2AI), First Name (FNAMEI of COUSR2AI), Last Name (LNAMEI of COUSR2AI), Password (PASSWDI of COUSR2AI), and User Type (USRTYPEI of COUSR2AI). The status/error message (WS-MESSAGE) is also cleared to SPACES. The cursor is repositioned to the User ID field (USRIDINL = -1). The screen is redisplayed in its cleared state.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Screen Fields on PF4
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the operator presses PF4, all input fields and messages on the User Update screen must be cleared, allowing the operator to start a fresh user lookup.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF12 on the User Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the PF12 key press
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does NOT perform any save operation or validation. It sets the destination program to 'COADM01C' (Administration Menu) and immediately transfers control to that program via XCTL with the current session communication area, discarding any unsaved changes on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return to Administration Screen Without Saving on PF12
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the operator presses PF12, the system must immediately navigate back to the Administration Menu screen without saving any changes, effectively cancelling the update operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed a key on the User Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The pressed key is not one of the supported keys: Enter, PF3, PF4, PF5, or PF12
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG = 'Y'), populates WS-MESSAGE with the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY), and redisplays the User Update screen with the current field values intact and the error message shown

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Key Press Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the operator presses any key that is not a supported function key (Enter, PF3, PF4, PF5, PF12), the system must notify the operator that the key is not valid for this screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined that navigation away from the User Update screen is required (triggered by PF3, PF12, or new session redirect)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the return-to-previous-screen navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system first checks if a destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) has been set; if it is LOW-VALUES or SPACES, it defaults to 'COSGN00C' (Sign-On screen). The system then records the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) as CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) as CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, resets the program context (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) to ZEROS, and transfers control to the destination program via XCTL with the full session communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigation to Previous or Default Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating away from the User Update screen, the system must determine the correct destination program and transfer control, defaulting to the Sign-On screen if no destination is specified.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Update program (COUSR2) has been launched and no communication area length is present (session length equals zero), indicating no active session exists
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates whether a valid session context was passed at program entry
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system determines that no valid session exists and initiates a redirect to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C), blocking access to all user update operations

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Missing Session on Program Launch
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User Update program is launched without an active session context (no communication area passed), the system must detect this condition and prevent access to user update operations by redirecting the user to the Sign-On screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has determined that no valid session context exists (communication area length is zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redirect the user away from the User Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The destination program is set to the Sign-On screen identifier 'COSGN00C' so that the subsequent navigation targets the correct authentication screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Sign-On Screen as Redirect Destination When No Session Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no valid session is detected at program launch, the system must explicitly set the navigation destination to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) before performing the redirect, ensuring the user is routed to authenticate first.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to redirect the user to a previous or target screen and the destination program field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) has been evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the destination program identifier contains a valid value (i.e., is not blank spaces and not low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the destination program is blank or unassigned (contains spaces or low-values), the system proceeds to apply a default destination; if the destination is already assigned with a valid program name, the system proceeds directly to record navigation details and execute the redirect

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate That a Redirect Destination Has Been Assigned
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before executing any navigation away from the User Update screen, the system must verify that a valid destination program has been assigned. This safeguard ensures the user is never redirected to an undefined or blank destination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is executing the return-to-previous-screen navigation logic and the destination program field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is found to contain spaces or low-values (i.e., no destination was explicitly set)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system applies the default destination rule
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The destination program is overridden and set to the Sign-On screen identifier 'COSGN00C', ensuring a valid navigation target is always present before the redirect is executed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Redirect Destination to Sign-On Screen When Destination Is Missing
all_rules.Rule_Description: As a safety policy, if the redirect destination is found to be unassigned or blank at the point of navigation, the system must default the destination to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C), ensuring the user is always routed to a valid and secure screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has confirmed a valid redirect destination and is preparing to transfer control to another screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system records navigation context details prior to executing the screen transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction identifier (WS-TRANID) is stored as the originating transaction (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is stored as the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), and the program context indicator is reset to zero (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT = 0) in the session communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Program and Transaction Details for Return Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to another screen, the system must record the current transaction ID, current program name, and reset the program context to zero in the session communication area. This ensures the destination screen knows where the user came from and can support correct back-navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination program has been confirmed and assigned (defaulted to COSGN00C if previously unset), and the current program and transaction details have been recorded in the session communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the screen transfer to the destination program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, which is 'COSGN00C' in this flow) and the full session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is passed to the destination screen, ensuring session continuity

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer User to Sign-On Screen via Program Control
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all navigation details have been recorded, the system must execute the actual transfer of control to the designated destination screen, passing the current session communication area so that session context is preserved across the screen transition.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user navigates to the User Update screen and the session communication area is present (session is active)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program detects that the screen has NOT been previously entered in this session (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER flag is not set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program marks the screen as entered (sets CDEMO-PGM-REENTER to TRUE), clears all screen output fields (COUSR2AO set to LOW-VALUES), and positions the cursor on the User ID input field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect First Entry into User Update Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the user is accessing the Update User screen for the first time in the current session, and initializes the screen state accordingly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Update screen is being loaded for the first time in the current session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks the pre-selected user value (CDEMO-CU02-USR-SELECTED) passed from the previous screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the pre-selected user value is NOT empty (not SPACES and not LOW-VALUES), the system proceeds to auto-populate the User ID field and look up the user's details; if the pre-selected user value IS empty (SPACES or LOW-VALUES), the system displays an empty update form for manual entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Check if a User ID Was Pre-selected from a Previous Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: On first entry to the Update User screen, determines whether a User ID was passed from a prior screen (e.g., an admin user list) to decide whether to auto-populate the form or display it empty.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Update screen is being loaded for the first time and a User ID was pre-selected from a previous screen (CDEMO-CU02-USR-SELECTED is not empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initializes the Update User form
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The pre-selected User ID value (CDEMO-CU02-USR-SELECTED) is automatically copied into the User ID input field (USRIDINI) on the Update User form

all_rules.Rule_Name: Auto-populate User ID Field from Pre-selected User
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a User ID has been pre-selected from a previous screen, that User ID is automatically transferred into the User ID input field on the Update User form, eliminating the need for the user to manually type it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User ID field has been auto-populated from a pre-selected user on the first entry to the Update User screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initializes the form with the pre-selected User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system automatically performs the user lookup process (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY) which reads the User Security file using the populated User ID as the search key, retrieving the user's stored record for display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Automatic User Record Lookup for Pre-selected User
all_rules.Rule_Description: After auto-populating the User ID from a pre-selection, the system automatically initiates a lookup of the user's record in the User Security file without requiring the user to press Enter.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A User ID has been looked up in the User Security file and the user record was found successfully (no error flag is set)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system retrieves the user's stored details from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the Update User form with the following fields from the retrieved record: First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME → FNAMEI), Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME → LNAMEI), Password (SEC-USR-PWD → PASSWDI), and User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE → USRTYPEI)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Pre-fill Update Form with Existing User Details on Successful Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user record is successfully found in the User Security file, all editable user details are retrieved and pre-filled into the corresponding fields on the Update User form.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user record has been successfully found in the User Security file and all user details have been pre-filled into the Update User form
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is ready to present the pre-filled form to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Update User screen is displayed with all user fields populated, and the message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates ...' is shown in a neutral color (DFHNEUTR) in the message area, prompting the user to make changes and save

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Update Form with Save Instruction After Successful User Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving and pre-filling the user's details, the system displays the Update User form with an instructional message guiding the user to press PF5 to save any modifications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A User ID was pre-selected from a previous screen and the system has attempted to look up that User ID in the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Security file lookup returns a 'not found' response (record does not exist for the given User ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error flag is set to 'Y' (WS-ERR-FLG), the error message 'User ID NOT found...' is displayed in the message area of the Update User screen, and the cursor is repositioned to the User ID input field to allow the user to enter a different User ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Error When Pre-selected User ID Is Not Found in Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system attempts to look up a pre-selected User ID in the User Security file but the record does not exist, an error message is displayed to inform the user that the specified User ID was not found.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Update screen is being loaded for the first time in the current session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The pre-selected user value (CDEMO-CU02-USR-SELECTED) is empty (SPACES or LOW-VALUES), meaning no user was passed from a previous screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Update User screen is displayed with all input fields empty (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type all blank), the cursor is positioned on the User ID field, and no pre-filled data or instructional message is shown — the user must manually enter a User ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Empty Update Form When No User Was Pre-selected
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no User ID was pre-selected from a previous screen, the Update User form is displayed empty, allowing the user to manually enter a User ID and look up the user they wish to update.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the User Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen display process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date, extracts the month (MM), day (DD), and last two digits of the year (YY), assembles them into MM-DD-YY format, and places the formatted date into the screen header date field (CURDATEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date and Format as MM-DD-YY
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User Update screen is about to be displayed, the system retrieves the current calendar date and formats it into MM-DD-YY format for display in the screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the User Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen display process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system time, extracts hours (HH), minutes (MM), and seconds (SS), assembles them into HH-MM-SS format, and places the formatted time into the screen header time field (CURTIMEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Time and Format as HH-MM-SS
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User Update screen is about to be displayed, the system retrieves the current system time and formats it into HH-MM-SS format for display in the screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the User Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system places the application title line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) into the first title field (TITLE01O), the application title line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) into the second title field (TITLE02O), the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) into the transaction name field (TRNNAMEO), and the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) into the program name field (PGMNAMEO) on the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Header with Application Titles, Transaction ID and Program Name
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the User Update screen, the system populates the screen header with the application title lines, the current transaction identifier, and the current program name to provide context to the operator.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current date has been formatted as MM-DD-YY and the current time has been formatted as HH-MM-SS
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system places the formatted date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) into the screen date display field (CURDATEO) and the formatted time (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) into the screen time display field (CURTIMEO) in the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Header with Formatted Current Date and Time
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the User Update screen, the system places the formatted current date (MM-DD-YY) and formatted current time (HH-MM-SS) into the corresponding screen header display fields.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the User Update screen and a message may or may not have been set in WS-MESSAGE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If WS-MESSAGE contains an error or informational message (e.g., 'User ID can NOT be empty...', 'User ID NOT found...', 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...', 'User [UserID] has been updated...', 'Please modify to update...', or an invalid key message), that message is placed into the screen message area (ERRMSGO); if WS-MESSAGE contains only spaces, the screen message area is displayed as blank

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Error or Informational Message on Screen When Present
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User Update screen is displayed, any error or informational message that has been set during processing is transferred to the screen message area so the operator can see it. If no message has been set, the message area remains blank (spaces).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header has been populated with current date, time, transaction ID, and program name, and any applicable message has been placed in the message area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the User Update screen to the operator's terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User Update form (map COUSR2A from mapset COUSR02) is displayed to the operator showing all user data fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type), the populated header information, and any error or informational message; the screen is fully refreshed (erased and rewritten) and the cursor is positioned at the designated input field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display User Update Form with All User Data Fields to Operator
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all header and message information has been populated, the complete User Update form is presented to the operator. The form displays all user data fields — User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type — along with the populated header and any message, and positions the cursor appropriately for operator input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has previously been presented with the User Update Form (the program is in re-entry mode, meaning the screen has already been displayed at least once in the current session)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The operator submits the User Update Form by pressing any key (Enter, PF3, PF4, PF5, PF12, or any other key)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures all data entered by the operator from the User Update screen map (COUSR2A / COUSR02 mapset) into the internal input data area (COUSR2AI), making the following fields available for processing: User ID (USRIDINI), First Name (FNAMEI), Last Name (LNAMEI), Password (PASSWDI), and User Type (USRTYPEI)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Operator Input from User Update Form
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an operator submits the User Update Form, the system must capture all data entered on the screen — including User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type — from the User Update screen map (COUSR2A) into the internal input area for further processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has submitted the User Update Form and the system is capturing screen input from the User Update screen map (COUSR2A)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen data is received into the internal input area (COUSR2AI)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID value entered by the operator is available in the USRIDINI field of the input area, ready to be used for user record lookup or update validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Receive User ID Field from User Update Form
all_rules.Rule_Description: The User ID field entered by the operator on the User Update Form is received as part of the screen data capture. This field identifies which user record is to be looked up or updated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has submitted the User Update Form and the system is capturing screen input from the User Update screen map (COUSR2A)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen data is received into the internal input area (COUSR2AI)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The First Name value entered or modified by the operator is available in the FNAMEI field of the input area, ready to be compared against the existing stored value and potentially saved to the User Security file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Receive First Name Field from User Update Form
all_rules.Rule_Description: The First Name field entered or modified by the operator on the User Update Form is received as part of the screen data capture. This field represents the user's first name to be updated in the User Security file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has submitted the User Update Form and the system is capturing screen input from the User Update screen map (COUSR2A)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen data is received into the internal input area (COUSR2AI)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Last Name value entered or modified by the operator is available in the LNAMEI field of the input area, ready to be compared against the existing stored value and potentially saved to the User Security file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Receive Last Name Field from User Update Form
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Last Name field entered or modified by the operator on the User Update Form is received as part of the screen data capture. This field represents the user's last name to be updated in the User Security file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has submitted the User Update Form and the system is capturing screen input from the User Update screen map (COUSR2A)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen data is received into the internal input area (COUSR2AI)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Password value entered or modified by the operator is available in the PASSWDI field of the input area, ready to be compared against the existing stored value and potentially saved to the User Security file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Receive Password Field from User Update Form
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Password field entered or modified by the operator on the User Update Form is received as part of the screen data capture. This field represents the user's password to be updated in the User Security file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has submitted the User Update Form and the system is capturing screen input from the User Update screen map (COUSR2A)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen data is received into the internal input area (COUSR2AI)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User Type value entered or modified by the operator is available in the USRTYPEI field of the input area, ready to be compared against the existing stored value and potentially saved to the User Security file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Receive User Type Field from User Update Form
all_rules.Rule_Description: The User Type field entered or modified by the operator on the User Update Form is received as part of the screen data capture. This field represents the user's role or type classification to be updated in the User Security file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All operator input has been successfully captured from the User Update Form into the internal input area (COUSR2AI)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the function key pressed by the operator at the time of form submission
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system routes processing as follows: if the operator pressed Enter — perform a User ID lookup to retrieve and display the user's current details; if the operator pressed PF3 — save any changes to the user record and then navigate back to the previous screen; if the operator pressed PF4 — clear all fields on the screen and redisplay an empty form; if the operator pressed PF5 — save any changes to the user record and remain on the User Update screen; if the operator pressed PF12 — navigate back to the Admin Menu without saving any changes; if any other key was pressed — display an invalid key error message and redisplay the current screen with all entered data intact

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route Processing Based on Key Pressed After Input Capture
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once all operator input has been successfully captured from the User Update Form, the system determines the appropriate processing action based on which function key the operator pressed when submitting the form. Each key triggers a distinct business operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator is on the Update User screen and has pressed the Enter key to initiate a user record lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID input field is empty (contains only spaces or no value at all)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the error flag to ON to indicate a validation failure, (2) Display the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...' on the screen, (3) Position the cursor on the User ID input field to guide the operator, (4) Redisplay the Update User screen with the error message visible, and (5) NOT proceed to look up any user record — the operator must enter a valid User ID before the lookup can continue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate User ID is Not Empty Before Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an operator presses Enter to look up a user record, the system must validate that the User ID field has been entered. If the User ID field is blank or contains no value, the system must prevent the lookup, display an error message, and prompt the operator to provide a valid User ID before proceeding.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has entered a User ID on the User Update screen and pressed Enter
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to look up the user record in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entered User ID from the update form (USRIDINI) is assigned as the record search key (SEC-USR-ID) to be used for the User Security File lookup

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set User ID as Search Key for Security File Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before searching the User Security File, the User ID entered by the operator on the update form must be assigned as the search key to identify the target user record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User ID has been set as the search key (SEC-USR-ID) for the User Security File lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs the user record lookup against the User Security File (USRSEC)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system searches the User Security File using the User ID as the record identifier and retrieves the full user data record (SEC-USER-DATA) if it exists, locking it for potential update

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve User Record from User Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must search the User Security File using the provided User ID to retrieve the existing user record. The record is retrieved in update mode to allow subsequent modifications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security File lookup has completed successfully and the user record was found
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No error condition is active (ERR-FLG-ON is false)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the User Update screen fields with the retrieved user data: First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME → FNAMEI), Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME → LNAMEI), Password (SEC-USR-PWD → PASSWDI), and User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE → USRTYPEI), and the updated screen is displayed to the operator

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Update Form with Retrieved User Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user record is successfully found in the User Security File, the system must populate all editable fields on the User Update screen with the current stored values for that user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security File lookup has completed and the user record was found successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the successful lookup response
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the screen message to 'Press PF5 key to save your updates ...' displayed in neutral color, and the User Update screen is refreshed to show this message along with the retrieved user data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Save Prompt Message After Successful User Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user record is successfully found and retrieved from the User Security File, the system must guide the operator by displaying an instructional message to press PF5 to save any modifications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has entered a User ID and the system has searched the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Security File lookup returns a 'record not found' result for the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active ('Y'), displays the error message 'User ID NOT found...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the User ID field to prompt correction, and redisplays the User Update screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Error When User ID Not Found in Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered User ID does not match any existing record in the User Security File, the system must notify the operator with a specific error message and direct them to correct the User ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security File lookup has returned a 'not found' result for the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the User Update screen with the error condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor length indicator for the User ID field (USRIDINL) is set to -1, which positions the cursor on the User ID input field when the screen is redisplayed, prompting the operator to re-enter a valid User ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight User ID Field for Correction After Not Found Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a User ID is not found in the User Security File, the system must direct the operator's attention back to the User ID field by positioning the cursor there, enabling immediate correction without additional navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file for the entered User ID, and no error condition is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the User Update screen for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The First Name field on the update form is populated with the stored First Name value retrieved from the User Security file record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate First Name Field with Stored Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving a user record from the User Security file, the First Name field on the update form must be pre-filled with the user's currently stored First Name so the operator can review and optionally modify it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file for the entered User ID, and no error condition is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the User Update screen for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Last Name field on the update form is populated with the stored Last Name value retrieved from the User Security file record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Last Name Field with Stored Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving a user record from the User Security file, the Last Name field on the update form must be pre-filled with the user's currently stored Last Name so the operator can review and optionally modify it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file for the entered User ID, and no error condition is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the User Update screen for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Password field on the update form is populated with the stored Password value retrieved from the User Security file record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Password Field with Stored Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving a user record from the User Security file, the Password field on the update form must be pre-filled with the user's currently stored Password so the operator can review and optionally modify it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file for the entered User ID, and no error condition is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the User Update screen for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User Type field on the update form is populated with the stored User Type value retrieved from the User Security file record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate User Type Field with Stored Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving a user record from the User Security file, the User Type field on the update form must be pre-filled with the user's currently stored User Type so the operator can review and optionally modify it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All four user data fields (First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type) have been populated from the successfully retrieved User Security file record, and no error condition is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the User Update screen to the operator
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The update form is displayed with all four fields pre-filled with current stored values, and an instructional message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates ...' is shown in neutral color, with the cursor positioned on the User ID field, allowing the operator to review and modify the pre-filled data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Pre-filled Update Form with Operator Guidance Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once all user fields (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) have been populated from the retrieved user record, the system must display the fully pre-filled update form to the operator along with a neutral-colored instructional message guiding them to press PF5 to save any modifications they wish to make.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Update User screen and has initiated a save action (via PF3 or PF5), and the User ID field contains only spaces or is blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins validating all required fields before saving the user record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the User ID input field, and returns the user to the Update User screen to correct the missing value — no save is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate User ID is Not Empty Before Saving User Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user attempts to save updates to a user record, the system must first verify that the User ID field has been provided. If the User ID is empty, the update is blocked and a specific error message is shown with the cursor directed to the User ID field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Update User screen and has initiated a save action (via PF3 or PF5), the User ID field is populated, and the First Name field contains only spaces or is blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to validate the First Name field as part of the sequential required-field validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'First Name can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the First Name input field, and returns the user to the Update User screen to correct the missing value — no save is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate First Name is Not Empty Before Saving User Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: After confirming the User ID is present, the system must verify that the First Name field has been provided before saving. If First Name is empty, the update is blocked and a specific error message is shown with the cursor directed to the First Name field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Update User screen and has initiated a save action (via PF3 or PF5), the User ID and First Name fields are populated, and the Last Name field contains only spaces or is blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to validate the Last Name field as part of the sequential required-field validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'Last Name can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the Last Name input field, and returns the user to the Update User screen to correct the missing value — no save is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Last Name is Not Empty Before Saving User Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: After confirming User ID and First Name are present, the system must verify that the Last Name field has been provided before saving. If Last Name is empty, the update is blocked and a specific error message is shown with the cursor directed to the Last Name field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Update User screen and has initiated a save action (via PF3 or PF5), the User ID, First Name, and Last Name fields are populated, and the Password field contains only spaces or is blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to validate the Password field as part of the sequential required-field validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'Password can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the Password input field, and returns the user to the Update User screen to correct the missing value — no save is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Password is Not Empty Before Saving User Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: After confirming User ID, First Name, and Last Name are present, the system must verify that the Password field has been provided before saving. If Password is empty, the update is blocked and a specific error message is shown with the cursor directed to the Password field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Update User screen and has initiated a save action (via PF3 or PF5), the User ID, First Name, Last Name, and Password fields are all populated, and the User Type field contains only spaces or is blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to validate the User Type field as the final step in the sequential required-field validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'User Type can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the User Type input field, and returns the user to the Update User screen to correct the missing value — no save is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate User Type is Not Empty Before Saving User Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: After confirming User ID, First Name, Last Name, and Password are present, the system must verify that the User Type field has been provided before saving. If User Type is empty, the update is blocked and a specific error message is shown with the cursor directed to the User Type field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Update User screen and has initiated a save action (via PF3 or PF5), and all five required fields — User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type — are populated with non-blank values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes the sequential validation of all required fields without encountering any empty field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error flag remains inactive, no error message is displayed, and the system proceeds to read the existing user record from the User Security file to compare current values against the entered values for change detection

all_rules.Rule_Name: All Required Fields Validated — Proceed to Detect and Save Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all five required fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type) are confirmed to be non-empty, the validation phase is complete and the system is authorized to proceed to the next step of comparing the entered values against the existing stored user record to detect any changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has passed all mandatory field validations (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type are all non-empty) and the system is ready to check for modifications
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the change detection process using the User ID entered on the Update User screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current user record from the User Security File using the entered User ID as the lookup key, making the stored First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type available for field-by-field comparison

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current User Record for Change Comparison
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before detecting any changes, the system must retrieve the current stored user record from the User Security File using the User ID entered by the operator, so that each entered field value can be compared against the stored values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security File and the stored First Name value is available for comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the First Name entered on the screen against the First Name stored in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the entered First Name is different from the stored First Name, the system updates the user record's First Name field with the newly entered value and sets the User Modified Flag to YES; if the values are identical, no change is recorded for First Name and the system proceeds to compare the Last Name

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in User First Name
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the First Name entered by the operator on the Update User screen against the First Name currently stored in the User Security File. If they differ, the First Name is marked as changed and the overall modification flag is set to indicate that at least one field has been updated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The First Name comparison step has been completed and the stored Last Name value is available from the retrieved user record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the Last Name entered on the screen against the Last Name stored in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the entered Last Name is different from the stored Last Name, the system updates the user record's Last Name field with the newly entered value and sets the User Modified Flag to YES; if the values are identical, no change is recorded for Last Name and the system proceeds to compare the Password

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in User Last Name
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the Last Name entered by the operator on the Update User screen against the Last Name currently stored in the User Security File. If they differ, the Last Name is marked as changed and the overall modification flag is set to indicate that at least one field has been updated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Last Name comparison step has been completed and the stored Password value is available from the retrieved user record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the Password entered on the screen against the Password stored in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the entered Password is different from the stored Password, the system updates the user record's Password field with the newly entered value and sets the User Modified Flag to YES; if the values are identical, no change is recorded for Password and the system proceeds to compare the User Type

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in User Password
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the Password entered by the operator on the Update User screen against the Password currently stored in the User Security File. If they differ, the Password is marked as changed and the overall modification flag is set to indicate that at least one field has been updated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Password comparison step has been completed and the stored User Type value is available from the retrieved user record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the User Type entered on the screen against the User Type stored in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the entered User Type is different from the stored User Type, the system updates the user record's User Type field with the newly entered value and sets the User Modified Flag to YES; if the values are identical, no change is recorded for User Type and the system proceeds to evaluate whether any field was modified overall

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in User Type
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the User Type entered by the operator on the Update User screen against the User Type currently stored in the User Security File. If they differ, the User Type is marked as changed and the overall modification flag is set to indicate that at least one field has been updated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All four field comparisons (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) have been completed and the User Modified Flag reflects whether any field value differed from its stored value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the User Modified Flag to determine the next course of action
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the User Modified Flag is YES (at least one field was changed), the system proceeds to save the updated user information to the User Security File; if the User Modified Flag is NO (no fields were changed), the system displays the warning message 'Please modify to update ...' highlighted in red on the Update User screen and does not perform any save operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Evaluate Overall Modification Status and Route to Appropriate Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all four fields have been compared, the system evaluates the overall User Modified Flag to determine whether any changes were actually made. If at least one field was changed, the system proceeds to save the updated user record. If no fields were changed, the system warns the operator that no modifications were detected and a save cannot be performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been retrieved from the User Security File and the user has entered values for First Name, Last Name, Password, and/or User Type on the Update User screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares each screen-entered value against the corresponding stored value: First Name on screen vs stored First Name, Last Name on screen vs stored Last Name, Password on screen vs stored Password, and User Type on screen vs stored User Type
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each field where the screen value does NOT match the stored value, the new value is staged for update and the record is flagged as 'modified'. If at least one field is flagged as modified, the system proceeds to write the updated record to the User Security File. If NO fields have changed, the system displays the message 'Please modify to update ...' in red and does NOT attempt to save the record.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Modified User Fields Before Save
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares each editable user field (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) entered on screen against the currently stored values in the User Security File. If any field differs from the stored value, that field is marked as changed and the overall record is flagged as modified, triggering the save process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user record has been flagged as modified (at least one of First Name, Last Name, Password, or User Type has changed) and the updated field values have been staged in the user data record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to rewrite the updated user record to the User Security File (USRSEC) using the existing record key (User ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete updated user record — including all modified and unmodified fields — is written to the User Security File, replacing the previously stored record for that User ID. The outcome (success, not found, or system error) determines the next step.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Updated User Record to User Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When at least one user field has been modified, the system rewrites the complete updated user record back to the User Security File (USRSEC), replacing the existing record for that User ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to rewrite the updated user record to the User Security File and the write operation completed successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Security File confirms the record was saved without error
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears any existing message text, sets the message color to green, builds the confirmation message in the format 'User [UserID] has been updated ...' where [UserID] is the actual User ID of the updated record (trimmed of trailing spaces), and displays this message on the Update User screen.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Success Confirmation After User Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon a successful save of the updated user record to the User Security File, the system clears any existing messages, builds a personalized confirmation message incorporating the User ID, and displays it on screen in green to confirm the update was completed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to rewrite the updated user record to the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Security File reports that the record for the given User ID was NOT found
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active ('Y'), displays the error message 'User ID NOT found...' on the Update User screen, and positions the cursor on the User ID field to prompt the user to re-enter or verify the User ID.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle User Not Found Error During Save
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the User Security File cannot locate the user record during the save (rewrite) operation — meaning the User ID no longer exists in the file — the system flags an error and displays an appropriate message to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to rewrite the updated user record to the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Security File returns an error response that is neither a successful save nor a 'User ID not found' condition (i.e., an unexpected system error)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active ('Y'), displays the error message 'Unable to Update User...' on the Update User screen, and positions the cursor on the First Name field. The user record is NOT updated in the system.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle System Error During User Record Save
all_rules.Rule_Description: If an unexpected system-level error occurs while attempting to save the updated user record to the User Security File (neither a successful save nor a 'not found' condition), the system flags an error and notifies the user that the update could not be completed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been retrieved and displayed on the Update User screen, and the user has not changed any of the fields (First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type on screen are all identical to the values stored in the User Security File)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether any field has been modified and determines that NO fields have changed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does NOT write to the User Security File, sets the message color to red, and displays the message 'Please modify to update ...' on the Update User screen, informing the user that at least one field must be changed before a save can be performed.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prevent Save When No User Data Has Been Modified
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the user attempts to save but has not changed any of the displayed user fields (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type all remain identical to the stored values), the system prevents an unnecessary write to the User Security File and prompts the user to make at least one change.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator is on the Update User screen with user details displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The operator presses PF5 to save and remain on the screen, OR presses PF3 to save and navigate back to the previous screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system initiates the Update User Info process, beginning with required field validations before any data is read or written

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger User Update Process on Save Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the operator presses PF5 (Save and Stay) or PF3 (Save and Navigate Back), the system initiates the user information update process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF5 or PF3 to save user information on the Update User screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs sequential validation of all required fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If User ID is empty, display error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...' and place cursor on User ID field; ELSE if First Name is empty, display error message 'First Name can NOT be empty...' and place cursor on First Name field; ELSE if Last Name is empty, display error message 'Last Name can NOT be empty...' and place cursor on Last Name field; ELSE if Password is empty, display error message 'Password can NOT be empty...' and place cursor on Password field; ELSE if User Type is empty, display error message 'User Type can NOT be empty...' and place cursor on User Type field; ELSE all validations pass and processing continues to retrieve the current user record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mandatory Field Validation Before Saving User Updates
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before saving any user updates, the system validates that all required fields are populated. Each field is checked in sequence and the first empty field encountered triggers an error message with cursor placement on that field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All required field validations have passed and no error flag is set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system looks up the User Security file using the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the user record is found, the current stored values for First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type are retrieved and held for field-by-field comparison; if the user is not found, display error message 'User ID NOT found...' and place cursor on User ID field; if a system error occurs, display error message 'Unable to lookup User...'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current User Record for Comparison
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all required field validations pass, the system retrieves the current user record from the User Security file using the entered User ID, locking it for update, before comparing entered values against stored values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the First Name entered on screen against the stored First Name value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the entered First Name is different from the stored First Name, the stored First Name is updated with the entered value and the record is marked as modified; if the entered First Name is the same as the stored value, no change is recorded for First Name and the system proceeds to check the Last Name field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in First Name Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the First Name entered by the operator against the currently stored First Name value in the User Security file to determine if a change has been made.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The entered First Name on the Update User screen is different from the First Name currently stored in the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects the First Name value has changed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The stored First Name is replaced with the newly entered First Name value, and the overall user record modification flag is set to 'Yes' indicating at least one field has changed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark First Name as Modified
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered First Name differs from the stored value, the system updates the First Name in the user record and flags the record as having been modified.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The First Name comparison has been completed (whether changed or unchanged)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the Last Name entered on screen against the stored Last Name value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the entered Last Name is different from the stored Last Name, the stored Last Name is updated with the entered value and the record is marked as modified; if the entered Last Name is the same as the stored value, no change is recorded for Last Name and the system proceeds to check the Password field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in Last Name Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the Last Name entered by the operator against the currently stored Last Name value in the User Security file to determine if a change has been made.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The entered Last Name on the Update User screen is different from the Last Name currently stored in the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects the Last Name value has changed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The stored Last Name is replaced with the newly entered Last Name value, and the overall user record modification flag is set to 'Yes' indicating at least one field has changed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Last Name as Modified
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered Last Name differs from the stored value, the system updates the Last Name in the user record and flags the record as having been modified.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Last Name comparison has been completed (whether changed or unchanged)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the Password entered on screen against the stored Password value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the entered Password is different from the stored Password, the stored Password is updated with the entered value and the record is marked as modified; if the entered Password is the same as the stored value, no change is recorded for Password and the system proceeds to check the User Type field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in Password Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the Password entered by the operator against the currently stored Password value in the User Security file to determine if a change has been made.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The entered Password on the Update User screen is different from the Password currently stored in the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects the Password value has changed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The stored Password is replaced with the newly entered Password value, and the overall user record modification flag is set to 'Yes' indicating at least one field has changed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Password as Modified
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered Password differs from the stored value, the system updates the Password in the user record and flags the record as having been modified.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Password comparison has been completed (whether changed or unchanged)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the User Type entered on screen against the stored User Type value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the entered User Type is different from the stored User Type, the stored User Type is updated with the entered value and the record is marked as modified; if the entered User Type is the same as the stored value, no change is recorded for User Type and the system proceeds to evaluate whether any fields were modified overall

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in User Type Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the User Type entered by the operator against the currently stored User Type value in the User Security file to determine if a change has been made.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The entered User Type on the Update User screen is different from the User Type currently stored in the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects the User Type value has changed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The stored User Type is replaced with the newly entered User Type value, and the overall user record modification flag is set to 'Yes' indicating at least one field has changed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark User Type as Modified
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered User Type differs from the stored value, the system updates the User Type in the user record and flags the record as having been modified.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All four user fields (First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type) have been compared against their currently stored values in the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks the overall modification flag to determine if any field was changed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If at least one field was marked as modified, the system proceeds to save the updated user record to the User Security file; if no fields were modified, the system displays a warning message to the operator without saving

all_rules.Rule_Name: Evaluate Whether Any User Fields Were Modified
all_rules.Rule_Description: After comparing all four user fields (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) against their stored values, the system evaluates whether at least one field was marked as modified to determine the next course of action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF5 or PF3 to save, all required field validations passed, the current user record was retrieved, and all four fields (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) were compared and found to be identical to their stored values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that the modification flag remains 'No' — meaning no field has been changed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does NOT write any changes to the User Security file, displays the message 'Please modify to update ...' highlighted in RED on the screen, and the operator remains on the Update User screen to review the warning and make necessary changes before attempting to save again

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Changes Detected Warning
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the operator attempts to save user information but none of the four fields (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) have been changed from their currently stored values, the system warns the operator that no update is needed and no write to the User Security file is performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: At least one of the four user fields (First Name, Last Name, Password, or User Type) has been marked as modified after comparison with stored values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system saves the updated user record to the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the save is successful, the screen displays a confirmation message 'User [UserID] has been updated ...' highlighted in GREEN; if the user record is not found during save, display error message 'User ID NOT found...' and place cursor on User ID field; if a system error occurs during save, display error message 'Unable to Update User...'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Persist User Updates to Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When at least one user field has been modified, the system writes the updated user record back to the User Security file and confirms the successful update to the operator.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator is on the Update User screen and presses PF3 to save and return to the previous screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID field is empty (contains spaces or no value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to ON, (2) display the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...' on the screen, (3) position the cursor on the User ID field, (4) remain on the Update User screen without saving or navigating away

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate User ID is Not Empty on PF3 Save and Return
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the operator presses PF3 to save and return, the User ID field must contain a value. If the User ID is empty, the save operation is blocked and an error is displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator is on the Update User screen, the User ID field is populated, and the operator presses PF3 to save and return
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The First Name field is empty (contains spaces or no value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to ON, (2) display the error message 'First Name can NOT be empty...' on the screen, (3) position the cursor on the First Name field, (4) remain on the Update User screen without saving or navigating away

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate First Name is Not Empty on PF3 Save and Return
