all_rules.Rule_Description: When the operator presses PF3 to save and return, the First Name field must contain a value. If First Name is empty, the save operation is blocked and an error is displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator is on the Update User screen, the User ID and First Name fields are populated, and the operator presses PF3 to save and return
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Last Name field is empty (contains spaces or no value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to ON, (2) display the error message 'Last Name can NOT be empty...' on the screen, (3) position the cursor on the Last Name field, (4) remain on the Update User screen without saving or navigating away

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Last Name is Not Empty on PF3 Save and Return
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the operator presses PF3 to save and return, the Last Name field must contain a value. If Last Name is empty, the save operation is blocked and an error is displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator is on the Update User screen, the User ID, First Name, and Last Name fields are populated, and the operator presses PF3 to save and return
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Password field is empty (contains spaces or no value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to ON, (2) display the error message 'Password can NOT be empty...' on the screen, (3) position the cursor on the Password field, (4) remain on the Update User screen without saving or navigating away

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Password is Not Empty on PF3 Save and Return
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the operator presses PF3 to save and return, the Password field must contain a value. If Password is empty, the save operation is blocked and an error is displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator is on the Update User screen, the User ID, First Name, Last Name, and Password fields are all populated, and the operator presses PF3 to save and return
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Type field is empty (contains spaces or no value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to ON, (2) display the error message 'User Type can NOT be empty...' on the screen, (3) position the cursor on the User Type field, (4) remain on the Update User screen without saving or navigating away

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate User Type is Not Empty on PF3 Save and Return
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the operator presses PF3 to save and return, the User Type field must contain a value. If User Type is empty, the save operation is blocked and an error is displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF3, all required fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) have passed validation, and no error flag is set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the current user record from the User Security File using the entered User ID as the key, and compares each of the four fields: First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type against their currently stored values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each field where the entered value differs from the stored value — First Name, Last Name, Password, or User Type — the system must: (1) update the in-memory user record with the new entered value, and (2) set the User-Modified indicator to YES. If none of the four fields differ, the User-Modified indicator remains NO

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compare Entered User Data Against Stored Values to Detect Modifications
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all required fields pass validation on PF3, the system retrieves the current stored user record from the User Security File and compares each entered field against the stored value to determine if any changes were made.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF3, all required fields have passed validation, the current user record has been read from the User Security File, and at least one field (First Name, Last Name, Password, or User Type) has been changed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User-Modified indicator is set to YES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) write the updated user record back to the User Security File, (2) clear any prior messages, (3) display a success confirmation message in green reading 'User [User ID] has been updated...' where [User ID] is the actual User ID value, (4) display the updated screen before proceeding to navigate away

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Updated User Record When Changes Are Detected on PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: When at least one user field has been modified compared to the stored record, the system saves the updated user record to the User Security File and displays a success confirmation message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF3, all required fields have passed validation, the current user record has been read from the User Security File, and none of the fields (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) differ from the stored values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User-Modified indicator remains set to NO
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) NOT write any record to the User Security File, (2) display the warning message 'Please modify to update ...' in red on the screen, (3) remain on the Update User screen and still proceed to navigate back to the calling program after displaying the warning

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Warning When No User Data Changes Are Detected on PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the operator presses PF3 but none of the user fields have been changed from their stored values, the system displays a warning message in red and does not perform a save operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF3 and the UPDATE-USER-INFO process has completed (either saved successfully, displayed a no-changes warning, or encountered a save error)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the calling program identifier stored in the session context (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the calling program identifier contains a valid program name (not spaces or empty), the system must transfer control to that calling program. If the calling program identifier is empty or contains only spaces, the system must transfer control to the Administration screen (COADM01C). In both cases, the current program name and transaction ID are recorded in the session context before transferring control

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate Back to Calling Program or Administration Screen After PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the save attempt (whether successful, no-changes warning, or validation error-free path), the system determines where to navigate: back to the program that originally called this screen, or to the Administration screen if no calling program is identified.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator is on the User Update form with any combination of data entered or displayed in the User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The operator presses the PF4 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID field is cleared to spaces and the cursor is set to the User ID field; the First Name field is cleared to spaces; the Last Name field is cleared to spaces; the Password field is cleared to spaces; the User Type field is cleared to spaces; all five fields are reset simultaneously as part of the same clear operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Input Fields on PF4 Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the operator presses PF4 on the User Update form, all input fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type) are cleared to spaces, and the cursor is repositioned to the User ID field, allowing the operator to start a fresh user lookup.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator is on the User Update form and there may be an existing error or status message displayed (e.g., 'User ID NOT found...', 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...', or any validation error message)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The operator presses the PF4 key, triggering the clear screen operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message area (WS-MESSAGE) is cleared to spaces; the error message display field (ERRMSGO) on the screen is set to spaces (reflecting the cleared WS-MESSAGE); no error or status message is shown on the refreshed screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Status and Error Messages on Screen Clear
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the operator presses PF4 to clear the User Update form, any existing status or error messages currently displayed on the screen are also cleared, ensuring the operator sees a completely blank and clean form with no residual messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All input fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) and all messages have been cleared following a PF4 key press
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The cleared User Update form is sent to the operator's screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is displayed with all input fields blank; the screen header is populated with the current date (MM/DD/YY format), current time (HH:MM:SS format), current transaction ID, and program name; the cursor is positioned on the User ID field; the message area is blank; the operator can immediately enter a new User ID to begin a fresh lookup

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Blank Update Form After Clear
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all input fields and messages have been cleared, the User Update form is refreshed and redisplayed to the operator in a completely blank state, with current date, time, transaction ID, and program name in the header, ready to accept a new User ID for lookup.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator is on the Update User screen with user data displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The operator presses the PF5 function key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system initiates the Update User Info process to validate all required fields and save any modifications to the User Security file, and the operator remains on the Update User screen after the operation completes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Save User Update on PF5 Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the operator presses the PF5 function key on the Update User screen, the system initiates the save user update process to validate and persist any changes made to the user record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF5 to save user updates on the Update User screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID field is empty or contains only spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag ON, displays the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the User ID field, redisplays the Update User screen, and does not proceed with any further validation or save operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate User ID is Not Empty Before Saving
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before saving user updates, the system must verify that the User ID field has been provided. The User ID is the key identifier for the user record and cannot be blank.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF5 to save user updates, and the User ID field is not empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The First Name field is empty or contains only spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag ON, displays the error message 'First Name can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the First Name field, redisplays the Update User screen, and does not proceed with any further validation or save operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate First Name is Not Empty Before Saving
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before saving user updates, the system must verify that the First Name field has been provided. First Name is a mandatory attribute of a user record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF5 to save user updates, and both User ID and First Name fields are not empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Last Name field is empty or contains only spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag ON, displays the error message 'Last Name can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the Last Name field, redisplays the Update User screen, and does not proceed with any further validation or save operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Last Name is Not Empty Before Saving
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before saving user updates, the system must verify that the Last Name field has been provided. Last Name is a mandatory attribute of a user record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF5 to save user updates, and User ID, First Name, and Last Name fields are all not empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Password field is empty or contains only spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag ON, displays the error message 'Password can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the Password field, redisplays the Update User screen, and does not proceed with any further validation or save operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Password is Not Empty Before Saving
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before saving user updates, the system must verify that the Password field has been provided. Password is a mandatory security attribute of a user record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed PF5 to save user updates, and User ID, First Name, Last Name, and Password fields are all not empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Type field is empty or contains only spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag ON, displays the error message 'User Type can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the User Type field, redisplays the Update User screen, and does not proceed with any further validation or save operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate User Type is Not Empty Before Saving
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before saving user updates, the system must verify that the User Type field has been provided. User Type is a mandatory classification attribute of a user record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All required fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) have passed validation and no error flag is set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system looks up the user record in the User Security file using the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the user record is found, the system retrieves the current stored values for First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type, displays the message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...' and proceeds to compare the screen values against the stored values; if the User ID is not found in the User Security file, the system displays the error message 'User ID NOT found...' and positions the cursor on the User ID field; if a system error occurs during the lookup, the system displays the error message 'Unable to lookup User...' and positions the cursor on the First Name field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Look Up Current User Record from User Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all required fields pass validation, the system retrieves the current user record from the User Security file using the entered User ID, to enable field-level comparison before saving updates.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The First Name value entered on the screen is different from the First Name currently stored in the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system updates the user record's First Name with the new value from the screen and marks the user record as modified

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in First Name Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: After retrieving the current user record, the system compares the First Name entered on screen against the stored First Name value to determine if an update is needed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Last Name value entered on the screen is different from the Last Name currently stored in the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system updates the user record's Last Name with the new value from the screen and marks the user record as modified

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in Last Name Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: After retrieving the current user record, the system compares the Last Name entered on screen against the stored Last Name value to determine if an update is needed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Password value entered on the screen is different from the Password currently stored in the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system updates the user record's Password with the new value from the screen and marks the user record as modified

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in Password Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: After retrieving the current user record, the system compares the Password entered on screen against the stored Password value to determine if an update is needed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Type value entered on the screen is different from the User Type currently stored in the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system updates the user record's User Type with the new value from the screen and marks the user record as modified

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in User Type Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: After retrieving the current user record, the system compares the User Type entered on screen against the stored User Type value to determine if an update is needed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed comparing all four fields (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) between the screen input and the stored user record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether any of the four fields were marked as modified
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If at least one field was modified, the system proceeds to save the updated user record to the User Security file; if no fields were modified, the system displays the warning message 'Please modify to update...' in red on the Update User screen and does not perform any save operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Whether Any User Fields Were Modified
all_rules.Rule_Description: After comparing all individual fields, the system determines whether at least one field was changed to decide whether to proceed with saving or to warn the operator that no changes were detected.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: At least one user field (First Name, Last Name, Password, or User Type) has been modified and marked for update
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system saves the updated user record to the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the save is successful, the system displays a success confirmation message in green reading 'User [User ID] has been updated...' on the Update User screen; if the User ID is not found during the save, the system displays the error message 'User ID NOT found...' and positions the cursor on the User ID field; if a system error occurs during the save, the system displays the error message 'Unable to Update User...' and positions the cursor on the First Name field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Updated User Record to User Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When at least one field has been modified, the system writes the updated user record back to the User Security file to persist the changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The updated user record has been successfully written to the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The save operation completes without errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays a success message in green color formatted as 'User [User ID] has been updated...' on the Update User screen, and the operator remains on the Update User screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Success Confirmation After Saving User Updates
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successfully saving the updated user record, the system provides a clear visual confirmation to the operator that the update was completed successfully.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has compared all fields and determined that none of the values (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) differ from the currently stored values in the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No fields have been marked as modified
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the warning message 'Please modify to update...' in red color on the Update User screen, does not write any record to the User Security file, and the operator remains on the Update User screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Warning When No User Fields Were Changed
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the operator attempts to save but has not changed any field values from what is already stored, the system warns the operator that a modification is required before an update can be performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator is on the User Update screen with or without unsaved changes
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The operator presses the PF12 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Administration Screen (COADM01C) and no user data is saved or updated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Destination to Administration Screen on PF12
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the operator presses PF12, the system sets the navigation destination to the main Administration Screen (COADM01C) without performing any save operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to navigate away from the User Update screen after PF12 is pressed and the destination program field has been set to COADM01C
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the destination program field contains a valid (non-blank, non-empty) value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the destination program is blank or uninitialized (LOW-VALUES or SPACES), the system overrides it and sets the destination to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C); if the destination is already set to a valid value such as COADM01C, the system retains that destination and proceeds with navigation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Destination Screen is Not Blank Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before navigating away from the User Update screen, the system validates that a destination screen has been set. If the destination is blank or uninitialized, the system defaults to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to ensure the operator is always directed to a valid screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination screen has been determined (either COADM01C or defaulted to COSGN00C) and the system is preparing to navigate
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the session communication data for transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction ID into the session's 'from transaction' field, records the current program name into the session's 'from program' field, resets the program context indicator to zero, and packages the full communication area to be passed to the destination screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve and Pass Current Session Context to Destination Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the destination screen, the system records the current transaction identity and program name into the session communication area, and resets the program context indicator to zero, ensuring the destination screen receives accurate session origin information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination screen is confirmed as COADM01C (or COSGN00C as fallback) and the session communication data has been prepared with the current transaction ID, program name, and reset context
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the navigation transfer to the destination program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is fully transferred to the destination screen with the communication area passed along, the User Update screen is exited, and no changes to user data (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) are saved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Destination Screen Without Saving Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: After setting the destination and preparing the session context, the system transfers full control to the destination screen (COADM01C or COSGN00C as fallback), passing the complete communication area. Any unsaved changes on the User Update screen are discarded as no save operation is performed during PF12 navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator is on the User Update screen and the system is ready to receive a key press
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The operator presses any key other than Enter, PF3, PF4, PF5, or PF12
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the Error Flag to active ('Y') to indicate an invalid key was pressed, blocking any further data processing actions

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Unsupported Key Press and Set Error State
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an operator presses a key that is not one of the supported function keys (Enter, PF3, PF4, PF5, PF12) on the User Update screen, the system must recognize it as an invalid action and activate the error state to prevent any unintended processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has pressed an unsupported key on the User Update screen and the error flag has been set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the unsupported key event
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system loads the standard invalid key message from CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY into the screen message field (WS-MESSAGE) to be displayed to the operator

all_rules.Rule_Name: Load Invalid Key Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unsupported key is detected, the system must load the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) into the screen message area to inform the operator which keys are valid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error flag is active and the invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) has been loaded into the message field, and the operator is on the User Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the User Update screen back to the operator
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the screen header with the current date (MM/DD/YY), current time (HH:MM:SS), transaction ID, and program name; places the invalid key error message in the error message display area (ERRMSGO) of the User Update screen (map COUSR2A, mapset COUSR02); and redisplays the screen with all previously entered data intact so the operator can review the valid key options

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay User Update Screen with Invalid Key Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: After detecting an unsupported key press and loading the invalid key message, the system must redisplay the User Update screen with the error message visible, along with refreshed header information (current date, time, transaction ID, and program name), so the operator can review valid key options and take appropriate action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Update User screen and a navigation-back action has been triggered, AND the session data contains no identified calling program (destination program is empty or uninitialized)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the destination program stored in the session communication area and finds it is blank or uninitialized
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) as the default navigation target

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default to Sign-On Screen When No Calling Program Is Identified
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system needs to return to a previous screen but no originating calling program has been recorded in the session, the destination defaults to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Update User screen and a navigation-back action has been triggered via PF3 or PF12, AND the session data contains a valid identified calling program or a specific destination has been assigned
Acceptance_Criteria.When: PF3 is pressed and a valid originating program is recorded in the session, the originating program is set as the destination; if no originating program is recorded, the Admin Menu (COADM01C) is set as the destination. When PF12 is pressed, the Admin Menu (COADM01C) is always set as the destination regardless of the originating program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The destination program in the session communication area is set to the identified calling program (originating program or Admin Menu COADM01C as applicable), and navigation proceeds to that destination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Use Identified Calling Program as Navigation Destination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system needs to return to a previous screen and a valid originating calling program is recorded in the session, that program is used as the navigation destination. The calling program may be explicitly set based on the key pressed (PF3 uses the originating program or defaults to Admin Menu; PF12 always uses Admin Menu).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined the destination program for navigation and is preparing to transfer control
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The return-to-previous-screen process is executing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current Transaction ID is recorded as the originating transaction in the session data, AND the current Program Name is recorded as the originating program in the session data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stamp Current Transaction ID and Program Name into Session Data Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the destination program, the system records the current transaction identifier and the current program name into the session communication area. This ensures the destination program knows which transaction and program initiated the navigation, maintaining a complete session trail.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has stamped the current transaction ID and program name into the session data and is preparing to transfer control to the destination program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The return-to-previous-screen process is executing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program context value in the session communication area is reset to zero, clearing any prior context state so the destination program begins in a clean initial state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Program Context to Fresh State Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the destination program, the system resets the program context indicator in the session data to zero (fresh/initial state). This ensures the destination program starts without inheriting any stale context flags from the current screen interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination program has been resolved (either the identified calling program or the default Sign-On screen COSGN00C), the current transaction ID and program name have been stamped into the session data, and the program context has been reset to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The return-to-previous-screen process completes its preparation steps
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is fully transferred to the destination program, and the complete session communication area (containing transaction ID, program name, program context, and all other session data) is passed to the destination program; the current program ceases execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Destination Program with Full Session Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: As the final step of the return navigation, the system transfers full control to the resolved destination program, passing along the complete session communication area. This ensures the destination program has access to all session context, including the originating transaction, program identity, and any other session state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A User ID has been entered on the Update User screen and all mandatory field validations have passed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates a lookup of the User Security File using the entered User ID as the unique search key, with the intent to lock the record for subsequent update
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User Security File is searched using the entered User ID, and the matching user record (containing First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type) is retrieved and held ready for comparison and potential update

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve User Record Using Entered User ID as Search Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system needs to retrieve a user's current record for update, it uses the User ID entered on the screen as the unique identifier to search the User Security File and lock the record for update.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security File has been searched using the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user record is found successfully in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current values of First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type from the User Security File record, and displays the informational message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...' on the screen in neutral color, keeping the Update User screen active

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Retrieved User Details and Prompt to Save
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user record is successfully found in the User Security File, the system retrieves all current user attribute values and instructs the user to press PF5 to save any modifications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security File has been searched using the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No matching user record is found in the User Security File for the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active ('Y'), displays the error message 'User ID NOT found...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the User ID field to prompt correction, and redisplays the Update User screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle User ID Not Found in User Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered User ID does not exist in the User Security File, the system must notify the user with a specific error message and direct focus back to the User ID field for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security File and the entered User ID is valid
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The First Name entered on the Update User screen is different from the First Name currently stored in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system replaces the stored First Name with the newly entered First Name and marks the user record as modified, indicating that a save operation is required

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in User First Name
all_rules.Rule_Description: After retrieving the current user record, the system compares the First Name entered on screen against the stored value to determine if a change has been made.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security File and the entered User ID is valid
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Last Name entered on the Update User screen is different from the Last Name currently stored in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system replaces the stored Last Name with the newly entered Last Name and marks the user record as modified, indicating that a save operation is required

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in User Last Name
all_rules.Rule_Description: After retrieving the current user record, the system compares the Last Name entered on screen against the stored value to determine if a change has been made.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security File and the entered User ID is valid
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Password entered on the Update User screen is different from the Password currently stored in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system replaces the stored Password with the newly entered Password and marks the user record as modified, indicating that a save operation is required

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in User Password
all_rules.Rule_Description: After retrieving the current user record, the system compares the Password entered on screen against the stored value to determine if a change has been made.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security File and the entered User ID is valid
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Type entered on the Update User screen is different from the User Type currently stored in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system replaces the stored User Type with the newly entered User Type and marks the user record as modified, indicating that a save operation is required

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in User Type
all_rules.Rule_Description: After retrieving the current user record, the system compares the User Type entered on screen against the stored value to determine if a change has been made.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid User ID exists in the User Security File, all mandatory fields (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) are non-empty, and at least one field value has been changed from the currently stored value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to save the updated user record to the User Security File using the User ID as the record key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The updated user record containing the modified First Name, Last Name, Password, and/or User Type values is written to the User Security File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Updated User Record to User Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all validations have passed and at least one user field has been modified, the system writes the updated user record back to the User Security File to persist the changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write the updated user record to the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The save operation completes successfully and the record is confirmed as updated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears any prior messages, constructs a confirmation message in the format 'User [UserID] has been updated ...' displayed in GREEN color, and redisplays the User Update screen with this success message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Success Confirmation After User Record Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User Security File is successfully updated, the system displays a green-colored confirmation message identifying the specific user that was updated, and returns the user to the User Update screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write the updated user record to the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The save operation fails because the User ID record no longer exists in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'User ID NOT found...', positions the cursor on the User ID field, and redisplays the User Update screen with the error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle User Not Found During Save Operation
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the user record no longer exists in the User Security File at the time of saving (e.g., the record was deleted between lookup and save), the system raises an error and returns the user to the User Update screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write the updated user record to the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The save operation fails due to an unexpected system error other than a missing record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'Unable to Update User...', positions the cursor on the First Name field, and redisplays the User Update screen with the error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle System Failure During User Record Save
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the save operation fails due to an unexpected system error (not a missing record), the system raises an error and returns the user to the User Update screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed the save operation to the User Security File with any outcome (success, user not found, or system failure)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The save result has been evaluated and the appropriate success or error message has been set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system redisplays the User Update screen (COUSR2A) with the current field values and the corresponding status or error message, keeping the user on the same screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return to User Update Screen After Save Attempt
all_rules.Rule_Description: Regardless of the outcome of the save operation (success, user not found, or system failure), the system always returns the user to the User Update screen with an appropriate message, ensuring the user remains in context to take further action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has entered a User ID value in the User ID field on the Update User form and all mandatory field validations have passed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to look up the user record in the User Security File for update verification
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must use the User ID value entered by the operator on the form (USRIDINI field) as the search key (SEC-USR-ID) to locate the corresponding user record in the User Security File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Use Entered User ID as Search Key for Update Verification Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before looking up a user record for update, the system must capture the User ID value entered by the operator on the Update User form and use it as the key to search the User Security File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has provided a User ID on the Update User form and the system is ready to retrieve the user record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system searches the User Security File (USRSEC) using the User ID as the record key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must read the user record from the User Security File with an exclusive update lock applied, ensuring the record is reserved for this update operation and cannot be modified by another process simultaneously

all_rules.Rule_Name: Search and Lock User Record in User Security File for Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must search the User Security File using the provided User ID and acquire an exclusive lock on the record to prevent concurrent modifications during the update process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched the User Security File using the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The search operation completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the user record is found successfully, the system must lock the record and proceed to display the current user data for comparison and update; if the user record is not found, the system must display an error and prompt the operator to re-enter the User ID; if a system error occurs during the search, the system must display an error message indicating the user could not be looked up

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Outcome Based on Whether User Record Was Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: After searching the User Security File, the system must evaluate whether the User ID exists in the file and route the process accordingly — either proceeding with the update or notifying the operator of the failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully located the user record in the User Security File using the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user record is found and the read-with-lock operation completes successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must lock the user record to prevent concurrent updates, display the message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...' in a neutral color on the Update User form, and return the current user data (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) to the form so the operator can review and modify the values

all_rules.Rule_Name: Lock User Record and Prompt Operator to Save Updates
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user record is successfully found in the User Security File, the system locks the record for exclusive update access and instructs the operator to press PF5 to save their modifications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user record has been successfully found and locked in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to display the Update User form with the retrieved user data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...' in neutral color in the message area of the Update User form, and populate the form fields with the retrieved values: First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME), Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME), Password (SEC-USR-PWD), and User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Save Prompt Message After Successful User Record Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successfully retrieving and locking the user record, the system must guide the operator by displaying an instructional message indicating how to save their changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The operator has entered a User ID on the Update User form and the system has searched the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID is not found in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the error indicator to active ('Y'), display the error message 'User ID NOT found...' in the message area of the Update User form, and position the cursor on the User ID field to prompt the operator to enter a valid User ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display User Not Found Error When User ID Does Not Exist in Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered User ID cannot be located in the User Security File during the update lookup, the system must notify the operator with a specific error message and highlight the User ID field for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User ID entered by the operator was not found in the User Security File and the error flag has been set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system redisplays the Update User form
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the Update User form with the error message 'User ID NOT found...' shown in the message area, the cursor positioned on the User ID input field (cursor length set to -1 on USRIDINL), and the header information (current date, time, transaction ID, program name) refreshed on the form

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Update Form with Error Highlighted on User ID Field When User Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a failed user lookup due to a non-existent User ID, the system must redisplay the Update User form with the error message visible and the cursor positioned on the User ID field so the operator can correct the entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user record has been successfully found and locked in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system redisplays the Update User form after a successful lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must populate the Update User form fields with the current stored values from the User Security File: First Name field with SEC-USR-FNAME, Last Name field with SEC-USR-LNAME, Password field with SEC-USR-PWD, and User Type field with SEC-USR-TYPE, along with the instructional message 'Press PF5 key to save your updates...' so the operator can compare and modify the values before saving

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Update Form with Current User Data Ready for Comparison
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving the user record, the system must populate the Update User form with the current stored values so the operator can review and modify them before saving.

description:
COUSR02C is a CICS online program within the CardDemo application that provides the functionality to update an existing user's information in the USRSEC security file. The program allows an administrator to look up a user by User ID and modify their first name, last name, password, and user type, validating all fields before saving changes. It operates as a Main/Driver program, managing its own screen interactions and navigating to other programs such as COADM01C via XCTL transfers.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: VSAM/CICS File (USRSEC) - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Session Initialization Check - When the program is first launched with no communication area, redirect the user to the sign-on screen (COSGN00C) to ensure a valid session exists before allowing any user update operations. 2: Initial Screen Load with Pre-selected User - On the first entry into the update screen, if a user ID has already been selected from a previous screen (CDEMO-CU02-USR-SELECTED), automatically populate the User ID field and look up the user's details to pre-fill the update form. 3: Display User Update Screen - Present the user update form to the operator, including header information (current date, time, transaction ID, program name), any error or informational messages, and the user data fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type). 4: Receive User Input from Screen - Capture all data entered by the operator on the user update form, including User ID and any modified fields for First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type. 5: Validate User ID on Lookup - When the operator presses Enter to look up a user, validate that the User ID field is not empty. If empty, display the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...' and prompt the operator to enter a valid User ID. 6: Look Up User Record - Using the entered User ID, retrieve the existing user record from the user security file. If the user is found, display a message prompting the operator to press PF5 to save updates. If the user is not found, display 'User ID NOT found...' error message. 7: Populate Screen with Existing User Data - After successfully retrieving the user record, populate the update form fields with the user's current First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type so the operator can review and modify them. 8: Validate All Required Fields Before Update - Before saving changes, validate that none of the required fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) are empty. Display specific error messages for each missing field: 'User ID can NOT be empty...', 'First Name can NOT be empty...', 'Last Name can NOT be empty...', 'Password can NOT be empty...', 'User Type can NOT be empty...' 9: Detect Changes to User Data - Compare each entered field value (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) against the current values stored in the user security file to determine if any modifications have been made by the operator. 10: Save Updated User Information - If one or more fields have been modified, write the updated user record back to the user security file and display a success message in green: 'User [ID] has been updated ...' 11: No Changes Detected Warning - If the operator attempts to save but no fields have been changed from their current values, display the message 'Please modify to update ...' in red to inform the operator that no update is needed. 12: Save and Return to Previous Screen (PF3) - When the operator presses PF3, attempt to save any user modifications and then navigate back to the calling program. If no calling program is identified, return to the administration screen (COADM01C). 13: Clear Screen Fields (PF4) - When the operator presses PF4, clear all input fields on the update form (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) and reset any messages, allowing the operator to start fresh. 14: Save User Updates (PF5) - When the operator presses PF5, validate all required fields and save any modifications made to the user's First Name, Last Name, Password, or User Type in the user security file. 15: Return to Administration Screen (PF12) - When the operator presses PF12, navigate back to the main administration screen (COADM01C) without saving any changes. 16: Invalid Key Handling - If the operator presses any key other than the supported function keys (Enter, PF3, PF4, PF5, PF12), display an invalid key message to inform the operator of the valid key options. 17: Return to Previous Screen Navigation - Transfer control back to the appropriate calling program, passing along the current session and communication data, defaulting to the sign-on screen if no calling program is specified.
